short_description: Why the Collatz (3x+1) conjecture resists proof: the map as a random walk, an optimizer and a Diophantine problem; proofs that fixed horizon monotone Lyapunov certificates and finite residue sieves cannot settle it and the cycle inequality cannot exclude all cycles; a momentum method from log2 3.
description:
The Collatz conjecture says that, from any positive integer, repeatedly halving an even number and sending an odd number n to 3n+1 always reaches 1. This book explains why the problem has resisted proof.

The conjecture splits into a divergence half, a law of large numbers along a single deterministic orbit, and a cycle half, a question about rational approximation of log2 3 that Diophantine information alone cannot finish. The book proves that no Lyapunov function increasing in the number certifies descent over any fixed number of steps, and that no finite residue sieve certifies descent for every integer. Infinitely many cycle lengths survive the cycle inequality, a point Halbeisen and Hungerbühler made earlier in another form; a sharp minimum inequality for rational cycles, nearly attained by Christoffel cycles, measures what a property of integers must add to exclude them. A seventeen state Turing machine that beeps forever exactly when the conjecture holds shows what one more quantifier costs. A tail criterion reduces the conjecture, given Lau's density theorem, to a polynomial bound.

Switching MM, a method that applies the momentum log2 3 minus 1 on alternate steps, has an explicit linear rate at step 1/L on smooth strongly convex functions, and on quadratics with additive gradient noise, at steps up to 1/L, its noise variance stays below 5/3 times that of gradient descent for every momentum coefficient below one. By the gain weight theorem, on quadratics with small steps no stable linear periodic first order method has a lower slow mode noise floor than gradient descent at matched speed. Beyond quadratics, at small steps, it runs at a fixed multiple of gradient descent's temperature.

Every result is proved in full or marked as conditional, and the Python scripts behind every computed number, figure and table are in the repository.

chapters.title: The $3x+1$ Problem
chapters.summary:
This chapter states the 3x+1 problem, also called the Collatz conjecture, the Syracuse problem, Kakutani's problem, Ulam's problem and Hasse's algorithm: halve an even integer, replace an odd integer n by 3n+1, and ask whether every positive integer reaches 1. It separates the two ways the conjecture can fail, a divergent orbit and a nontrivial cycle (the divergence half and the cycle half), introduces the standard, accelerated and Syracuse maps and stopping times, and works examples such as the orbit of 27, which takes 111 steps and peaks at 9232. It surveys computer verification up to 2^71 and the lower bounds on the length of a nontrivial cycle that it gives through the continued fraction of log base 2 of 3, the undecidability of generalized Collatz maps (Conway, FRACTRAN), and density theorems for stopping times, from Terras and Everett to Tao's almost bounded values and the positive density theorems of 2026. It explains the parity heuristic, a random walk for log x with drift log(sqrt(3)/2), and why it is not a proof: the parities along one orbit are deterministic. It describes the Lean statements of the conjecture, of its descent form and of the cycle problem written by the authors. It ends with the plan of the book, which does not prove the conjecture but reads it through martingales, optimization and Diophantine approximation.

#### From the literature

The survey of Lagarias (1985) and the volume he edited (2010); the density theorem for stopping times of Terras (1976, 1979) and Everett (1977); the exponent log 3 over log 4 of Korec (1994); the x to the power 0.84 bound of Krasikov and Lagarias (2003); the almost bounded values theorem of Tao (2022); the positive density theorems of the preprints of Mazur (2026), Shaik (2026) and Lau (2026), not yet refereed; the undecidability results of Conway (1972, 1987) and Kurtz and Simon (2007); computer verification by Oliveira e Silva (2010) and Bařina (2021, 2025); cycle length bounds from the continued fraction of log base 2 of 3 by Crandall (1978), Eliahou (1993) and Hercher (2023); the parity heuristic of Crandall (1978) and Lagarias and Weiss (1992).

#### New results

This chapter is an introduction and survey, and its labeled statements are the conjecture itself and a theorem of Tao (2022).

chapters.title: Parity Vectors and the Syracuse Map
chapters.summary:
This chapter isolates the parity test in the 3x+1 problem and asks what it determines for whole families of starting values. It fixes the standard, accelerated and Syracuse maps, defines the parity vector of an orbit, and proves the theorem of Terras and Everett: the parity vector of length k and the residue modulo 2^k determine each other, so a uniformly random residue gives k independent fair coin flips exactly. It then proves the affine form of k iterates, an explicit inverse of the parity vector map, the cycle formula, the exact Geometric law of the halving exponent v_2(3n+1) and the exact Syracuse drift log(3/4). In the 2 adic integers the Collatz map is conjugate to the Bernoulli shift, Haar measure is invariant, and the conjecture says that every positive integer has a parity vector ending in the tail 1010 and so on. The chapter then treats the stopping time and the coefficient stopping time of Terras with their exact counts, and proves the density theorem: integers with finite stopping time have natural density one, with the density of integers whose stopping time exceeds k at most e to the power minus Dk for a Kullback and Leibler divergence D of about 0.0347. All of this concerns ensembles of starting values, not a single orbit.

#### From the literature

The bijection between parity vectors and residues modulo 2^k of Terras (1976) and Everett (1977); the density theorem of Terras (1976, 1979) and Everett (1977) with the exponential bound of Lagarias (1985); the coefficient stopping time, its exact counts and its conjecture, all of Terras (1976); the conjugacy to the shift of Lagarias (1985), with mixing as a case of a theorem of Matthews and Watts (1984); the explicit inverse of Bernstein (1994); the periodicity conjecture of Lagarias (1985, 1990); the affine identity, cycle formula and Geometric law, which are classical.

#### New results

The results of this chapter are classical and credited to their authors in the text, so none is catalogued as new.

No new results of this chapter are catalogued.

chapters.title: Stochastic Models and Martingale Duality
chapters.summary:
This chapter asks what the probabilistic heuristic for the 3x+1 problem predicts and what martingale theory can prove about it. It defines three stochastic models of the Collatz iteration: the Bernoulli fair coin model for the accelerated map, the Geometric stride model for the Syracuse map, and a renewal (Markov chain) model for the standard map, where an odd step is always followed by a halving. In the Bernoulli model the iterates form a multiplicative martingale, because one half times one half plus one half times three halves equals one, while their logarithms form a supermartingale with drift log(sqrt(3)/2), about minus 0.1438, which is the Jensen gap (martingale duality). Wald's identity gives the slope 1/|drift|, about 6.952, of the expected passage time, the model's prediction for total stopping times, classical first passage results give its dispersion, Ville's maximal inequality bounds an excursion by a factor K with probability at most 1/K, and the model is absorbed almost surely. In the renewal model for the standard map the parity autocorrelation is exactly (minus one half) to the power h. The stopped martingale is not uniformly integrable, which shows why it cannot be used to settle absorption, even in the model. The predictions are compared with orbits, a census of all n below 2^30 places most of the ten percent variance deficit of total stopping times at the end of the orbit, and the chapter asks what a certificate for individual orbits would need.

#### From the literature

The fair coin picture of Terras (1976) and Everett (1977); the parity heuristic of Crandall (1978) and its drift log(sqrt(3)/2), recorded by Lagarias (1985); the random walk models of Lagarias and Weiss (1992); the structure theorem of Kontorovich and Sinai (2002) and the survey of Kontorovich and Lagarias (2010); the first passage asymptotics of Heyde (1967) and Siegmund (1969) and the normal limit for this model of Borovkov and Pfeifer (2001); Wald's identity (Wald 1944); the maximal inequality for nonnegative supermartingales of Ville (1939); the Lundberg inequality of risk theory, as treated by Asmussen and Albrecher (2010).

#### New results

The Bernoulli drift is classical; the authors' statements are elementary closed forms for the renewal model and the failure of uniform integrability.

- [Martingale structure of the renewal model for the standard Collatz map](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#martingale_structure_of_the_standard_map) (Proposition 3.7, page 45; proved): In the renewal model of the standard Collatz map, where every tripling is followed by a halving, the iterates are not a martingale, but they become one once each coming tripling is booked in advance. New in this book.
- [Exact parity autocorrelation function of the renewal model for the standard Collatz map](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#parity_autocorrelation_function) (Proposition 3.12, page 54; proved): In the renewal model of the standard Collatz map one step in three is odd and the parity autocorrelation at lag h is minus one half raised to the power h. New in this book.
- [Long run variance of the log path in the renewal model for the standard Collatz map](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#long_run_variance_of_the_log_path) (Corollary 3.14, page 55; proved): The negative parity correlations of the renewal model cut the long run variance of the log path to one third of its value for independent parities with the same frequency, one in three, of odd steps. New in this book.
- [The stopped martingale of the Bernoulli model is not uniformly integrable](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#failure_of_uniform_integrability) (Proposition 3.17, page 59; proved): The martingale of the Bernoulli model, stopped when the iterate first drops to 1 or below, is not uniformly integrable, because the unabsorbed paths keep expected value at least the starting value minus 1 while their probability tends to zero. New in this book.

chapters.title: Lyapunov Functions and the Limits of Descent
chapters.summary:
This chapter asks whether the heuristic that log x decreases on average along a 3x+1 (Collatz) orbit can be turned into a Lyapunov function, a potential certifying that every orbit reaches 1. It defines Lyapunov certificates for discrete maps, gives a discrete criterion and Foster's drift criterion for Markov chains, and shows that a certificate exists if and only if the Collatz conjecture holds. The positive results are the stride descent theorem for the Syracuse map, an exact two stride analysis, and bounds on the expected passage time of the stride model with its overshoot, from Wald's identity. The negative results are three obstructions. No strictly increasing function of x is a strict or strong Lyapunov function for one stride, because every x congruent to 3 mod 4 ascends. No monotone certificate over any fixed number of strides exists, because runs of ascending strides can be arbitrarily long. In majorization minimization (MM), the tangent line majorizer of log x has a surrogate that drifts upward while log x drifts downward in the model, and power majorizers with exponent below the Wald root 1 repair the drift in the model but not the pointwise failure.

#### From the literature

Lyapunov (1892, English translation 1992) for Lyapunov functions and LaSalle (1986) for discrete systems; Foster (1953) and Meyn and Tweedie (1993) on drift criteria; the heuristic for log x of Terras (1976), Crandall (1978) and Lagarias and Weiss (1992); the density theorem of Terras (1976) and Everett (1977); the equivalence of the conjecture with finiteness of every stopping time, folklore implicit in Terras (1976), see Lagarias (1985, 2010); the classical identity for runs of ascents (Terras 1976; Hercher 2023); the MM principle of Lange, Hunter and Yang (2000) and Hunter and Lange (2004).

#### New results

The new results are the stride descent theorem, the two stride analysis, the passage time bounds, the power majorizers and three obstructions to certificates.

- [Passage time of the stride model with overshoot](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#stride_model_passage_time) (Proposition 4.5, page 67; proved): In the random stride model of the Collatz map, the expected number of strides for log x to fall to zero or below is the starting log x plus the mean overshoot, which lies between log 2 and 2 log 2, divided by log(4/3), the size of the drift. New in this book.
- [Stride descent theorem for the Syracuse map](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#stride_descent) (Theorem 4.7, page 69; proved): One Syracuse stride lowers log x exactly when the halving exponent is at least 2 and raises it exactly when x is 3 mod 4, with sharp bounds on the size of the change. New in this book.
- [No monotone strong Lyapunov function for a single Syracuse stride](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#no_monotone_single_stride_lyapunov) (Theorem 4.8, page 71; proved): No strictly increasing function of x is a strict or strong Lyapunov function for the Syracuse map, because every integer congruent to 3 mod 4, half of all odd integers, ascends in one stride. New in this book.
- [Exact behaviour of two Syracuse strides](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#exact_two_stride_behaviour) (Proposition 4.12, page 72; proved): Over two Syracuse strides an odd integer decreases exactly when the two halving exponents sum to at least 4, which holds for half of the odd integers, and the largest two stride ascent is log(17/7), attained only at 7. New in this book.
- [No fixed horizon monotone certificate for Collatz descent](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#no_fixed_horizon_monotone_certificate) (Corollary 4.15, page 76; proved): For every fixed number J of strides, no strictly increasing function of x certifies descent over J Syracuse strides, because the odd integers congruent to minus 1 modulo 2 to the J+1 ascend for J strides in a row. New in this book.
- [The linear majorizer of log cannot certify Collatz descent](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#linear_majorizer_cannot_certify_descent) (Proposition 4.19, page 78; proved): In the stochastic model the tangent line majorizer of log x has a positive mean increment per step of the standard map while log x has a negative one, so the linear surrogate cannot certify descent. New in this book.
- [Power majorizers of log and the Wald root of the stride model](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#power_majorizers_of_log) (Proposition 4.20, page 79; proved): In the stride model the power majorizers of log with exponent strictly between 0 and 1 have strictly negative mean increment, interpolating between the true drift log(3/4) and the zero drift of the linear majorizer at the Wald root 1. chapters.title: Majorization and Momentum
chapters.summary:
This chapter turns from descent to momentum methods in optimization and asks which analogies between momentum and the Collatz orbit mean something. It reviews Polyak's heavy ball method and Nesterov's accelerated gradient method on strongly convex quadratics, including the optimal constant momentum coefficient for condition number kappa, and the continuous time view in which momentum is a damped oscillator certified by an energy with a kinetic term. The Collatz orbit is read as momentum injection by the odd step followed by correction by the halvings, with the orbit of 27 as an example. The ratio of the largest stride ascent to the mean stride descent is about 1.776, a ratio of increments and not a condition number, and mixing constants defined at different levels produces spurious agreements. The number beta equal to log base 2 of 3 minus 1, about 0.585, appears as an ascent to descent ratio, the excess over one of the Cesàro threshold for halvings per odd step, a rewriting of drift constants, and a ratio of Kullback and Leibler divergences. Parrondo's paradox illustrates state dependent switching, and beta becomes the momentum coefficient of Switching MM.

#### From the literature

The heavy ball method of Polyak (1964, 1987). The accelerated gradient method of Nesterov (1983, 2004). The optimal constant momentum on quadratics, classical, see Nesterov (2004). The failure of heavy ball to converge globally, from Lessard, Recht and Packard (2016). The differential equation of Su, Boyd and Candès (2016) and the high resolution equations of Shi, Du, Jordan and Su (2022). Lyapunov analysis of acceleration by Wilson, Recht and Jordan (2021) and adaptive restart by O'Donoghue and Candès (2015). Parrondo's games as published by Harmer and Abbott (1999), with Parrondo, Harmer and Abbott (2000) and the review of Harmer and Abbott (2002). An identity of Tao (2022) on the residue chain.

#### New results

The one labeled proposition of the chapter, the optimal constant momentum on quadratics, is classical, and the constants and identities are elementary.

No new results of this chapter are catalogued.

chapters.title: Majorization Pressed Harder
chapters.summary:
This chapter presses majorization minimization (MM) as far as it goes on the Collatz map. The multiplicative majorizer of a Syracuse stride, summed around a cycle, gives the cycle inequality, and its minorizer is the window lemma, so the cycle half becomes a question of how tight the majorizer can be made along a closed orbit. For the divergence half the chapter proves impossibility results for pointwise potentials. A potential log x plus a function of the residue modulo 2 to the d cannot decrease at every step for all large x, for any d, by a negative cycle criterion from shortest path theory: the residue graph has cycles of positive weight, the loop at minus 1 and the images of the cycles of the map on negative integers, and its maximum cycle mean is log of 3 over 2, attained by the loop. Any potential log x plus a correction that decreases at every stride needs a surplus growing linearly in the number of trailing ones of x. Block majorization over a run of ascents gives an exact block map and a renewal process under the model, but run length potentials fail at a fraction of odd integers that no weight brings below 0.143 in the model. In expectation, majorization is the supermartingale method.

#### From the literature

The negative cycle criterion is the Bellman and Ford condition of shortest path theory (Ford 1956, Bellman 1958), and the maximum cycle mean is computed by the algorithm of Karp (1978). The parity vector theorem of Terras (1976) and Everett (1977). The cycle identity and the cycles of the map on negative integers are classical, see Lagarias (1985). The classical identity for runs of ascents, see Hercher (2023), who cites Terras (1976). Steiner (1978) showed that the trivial cycle is the only cycle consisting of a single block, a circuit, see also Lagarias (1985).

#### New results

The new results are the residue potential theorem, the surplus along chains and the run length potential; the cycle identity and the block map are classical.

- [No residue potential for the Collatz map at any modulus](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#no_residue_potential_for_any_modulus) (Theorem 6.3, page 99; proved): No potential made of log x plus a function of residues modulo a power of 2 decreases at every step of the accelerated Collatz map for all large x, because the residue graph has cycles of positive weight, such as the loop at minus 1. New in this book.
- [Surplus of a pointwise potential along runs of trailing ones](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#surplus_along_chains) (Proposition 6.4, page 101; proved): A potential log x plus a correction that decreases at every Syracuse stride needs an unbounded correction, with a surplus growing linearly in the number of trailing ones of x. New in this book.
- [Run length potential and its failure fraction](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#run_length_potential) (Proposition 6.6, page 102; proved): With weight c above log(3/2), the run length potential log x plus c times the 2 adic valuation of x+1 decreases at all but finitely many ascending strides, but under the stride model it fails to decrease at a positive fraction of odd integers, 0.2087 at weight c equal to 1. New in this book.

#### Key terms

chapters.title: Switching MM
chapters.summary:
This chapter asks whether the momentum coefficient of a first order method can be fixed in advance, without knowing the condition number, and what such a default achieves. It derives the coefficient log(3/2)/log 2, which equals log2 3 minus 1 and is about 0.585, in two ways: from the Collatz map, as the ratio of the ascent of an odd step to the descent of a halving (the log displacement identity of the Syracuse map), and from elementary information theory, as a ratio of Kullback and Leibler divergences of nested uniform laws. The resulting method, Switching MM (SMM), applies Nesterov extrapolation only on odd iterations and a plain gradient step on even ones, with step size one over L. The main results are exact. For every differentiable function, two SMM steps from an even index are a gradient step of length (1+beta) alpha followed by one of length alpha. On strongly convex quadratics SMM is therefore a period two cyclic step size method with an explicit stability range and linear rate, and in the slow modes it acts like gradient descent with a step enlarged by (2+beta)/2, so it is not an accelerated method. A defect bound covers nonquadratic objectives with Lipschitz Hessian. The chapter states that the arithmetic bears nothing on the Collatz conjecture.

#### From the literature

Heavy ball momentum (Polyak 1964, 1987) and accelerated gradient (Nesterov 1983, 2004); the limit cycle of tuned heavy ball (Lessard, Recht and Packard 2016); the Adam default momentum 0.9 (Kingma and Ba 2015); differential equation views of acceleration (Su, Boyd and Candès 2016; Shi, Du, Jordan and Su 2022); cyclic and Chebyshev step sizes (Richardson 1911; Young 1953; Golub and Varga 1961) and the silver stepsize schedule (Altschuler and Parrilo 2025); MM algorithms (Lange, Hunter and Yang 2000; Hunter and Lange 2004); switched linear systems (Liberzon 2003).

#### New results

- [The extrapolated point of Switching MM is a long gradient step](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#extrapolated_point_is_a_long_gradient_step) (Lemma 7.5, page 115; proved): For every differentiable objective, two consecutive steps of Switching MM from an even index are exactly a long gradient step, longer by the factor one plus the momentum coefficient, followed by a plain gradient step. New in this book.
- [Two step equivalence of Switching MM with cyclic gradient steps on quadratics](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#smm_two_step_equivalence_on_quadratics) (Theorem 7.6, page 116; proved): On a strongly convex quadratic, two steps of Switching MM from an even index equal a plain gradient step followed by a longer one, so the method is a cyclic step size method and every two steps its error is multiplied by an explicit degree two polynomial of the Hessian. New in this book.
- [Stability range and linear convergence of Switching MM on quadratics](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#smm_stability_range_on_quadratics) (Corollary 7.8, page 117; proved): Switching MM converges linearly on every strongly convex quadratic for any momentum coefficient below one and step at most one over L, and it is stable exactly for normalized steps below an explicit limit. New in this book.
- [Slow mode effective step of Switching MM on quadratics](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#smm_slow_mode_effective_step) (Corollary 7.9, page 118; proved): In the slow directions Switching MM behaves like gradient descent with a step enlarged by the factor two plus beta over two, about 1.29 at the Collatz momentum, so it is not an accelerated method. New in this book.
- [Third order defect of the cyclic step representation of Switching MM](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#smm_defect_of_cyclic_representation) (Proposition 7.10, page 120; proved): For objectives with a Lipschitz Hessian, the failure of the odd iterates of Switching MM to follow a cyclic gradient path is of third order in the step size, and it vanishes for quadratics. New in this book.

chapters.title: Noise, Variance and Experiments
chapters.summary:
This chapter tests whether the parity schedule of Switching MM acts as a variance filter, using exact stationary variances on strongly convex quadratics with additive gradient noise and, for Switching MM, multiplicative noise. Every step heavy ball and Nesterov momentum are autoregressions of order two (AR(2)); on even iterates Switching MM reduces to an autoregression of order one, which gives exact variances for even, odd and phase averaged iterates. In the slow modes the noise amplification relative to gradient descent at the same step is (2+2beta+beta^2)/(2+beta), below 5/3 for every beta below one, a bound that holds on every eigendirection at step one over L, whereas every step momentum amplifies by 1 over (1 minus beta). At matched slow mode speed Switching MM has no advantage over gradient descent in the slow modes, although it is quieter in the fast ones, and the gain weight theorem shows that in the slow mode limit no stable linear periodic first order method beats gradient descent at matched speed: the noise floor is a Cauchy and Schwarz ratio of gains, equal to one only for equal gains. The chapter also gives the Pareto frontier between rate and noise for period two step ratios, ending at the Chebyshev schedule, and a mean square stability threshold under multiplicative noise. Experiments on quadratics, logistic regression and minibatch gradients, against heavy ball, Nesterov and Adam, are reconciled with the theory. Section 8.9 goes beyond quadratics: over strongly convex smooth functions the stationary error of Switching MM stays below five thirds of that of gradient descent for small fluctuations, and in the limit of small steps at fixed temperature the stationary laws converge to Gibbs laws at temperature V(beta) T and T (the temperature law), with ratio at most V(beta) cubed in one dimension and a ten ninths cap on the penalty of averaging; Problem S5 asks for the supremum of the ratio.

#### From the literature

Stationary variance of an autoregression of order two through the Yule and Walker equations (Brockwell and Davis 1991); heavy ball on quadratics (Polyak 1987); equivalence of momentum SGD and SGD with a rescaled step at small step sizes (Yuan, Ying and Sayed 2016); heavy ball and Nesterov need not improve on SGD for least squares (Kidambi, Netrapalli, Jain and Kakade 2018); the period two Chebyshev schedule (Young 1953; Golub and Varga 1961); Adam (Kingma and Ba 2015); the Breast Cancer Wisconsin data (Wolberg, Street and Mangasarian 1995).

- [Exact stationary variance of Switching MM under additive gradient noise](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#smm_stationary_variance_additive_noise) (Theorem 8.4, page 126; proved): An exact formula for the stationary variance of Switching MM on a quadratic with additive gradient noise, for even iterates, odd iterates and their phase average, as a rational function of the normalized step and the momentum coefficient. New in this book.
- [Slow mode noise amplification of Switching MM](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#smm_slow_mode_noise_amplification) (Corollary 8.5, page 127; proved): In the slow modes Switching MM amplifies gradient noise, relative to gradient descent at the same step, by an explicit function of the momentum coefficient that equals 1.359 at the Collatz value. New in this book.
- [Noise bound for Switching MM uniform in the normalized step](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#smm_variance_bound_uniform_in_normalized_step) (Proposition 8.7, page 128; proved): On a quadratic with additive gradient noise, on every eigendirection with normalized step up to one, the stationary variance of Switching MM lies between that of gradient descent and 5/3 times it, uniformly over momentum coefficients below one, whereas every step momentum amplifies slow mode noise by a factor that grows without bound as the coefficient tends to one. New in this book.
- [Noise floor at matched speed for momentum methods and Switching MM](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#noise_floor_at_matched_speed) (Proposition 8.9, page 130; proved): At matched slow mode speed Switching MM pays a small noise floor penalty over gradient descent, 1.051 at the Collatz momentum and at most 10/9; it is the period two analogue of the result of Yuan, Ying and Sayed (2016) that every step heavy ball and Nesterov match gradient descent exactly. New in this book.
- [Gain weight theorem for the noise floor of periodic first order methods](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#gain_weight_theorem) (Theorem 8.12, page 133; proved): For any linear periodic first order method on a quadratic that is stable at zero normalized step and has positive total gain, the slow mode noise floor at matched speed relative to gradient descent is a Cauchy and Schwarz ratio of the step gains, at least one, and equal to one only when all gains are equal. chapters.title: Nonlinear Difference Equations and Momentum MM
chapters.summary:
This chapter studies the nonlinear difference equations behind both halves of the book: the Collatz recursion as a switched system, and Switching MM as a momentum MM scheme. For Collatz, the proportion of odd steps decides whether an orbit grows, with threshold 1/log2 3, and a simplified version of the Krasikov difference inequality method on the inverse tree certifies growth exponents up to 0.477 (residues modulo 3^7) for the integers whose orbit passes through a given number not divisible by 3 and not on a cycle, below the 0.84 of Krasikov and Lagarias. For optimization, Switching MM with step one over L decreases the objective on alternate iterates for every L smooth function. The joint spectral radius of its descent and injection matrices is computed exactly because the descent matrix has rank one; a transient bound is stated as a conjecture, and conditionally on it every switching rule is exponentially stable on quadratics. For mu strongly convex, L smooth functions, two steps contract the distance to the minimizer by an explicit factor, which is the exact worst case, confirmed by performance estimation (PEP). A modified equation shows that Switching MM has no inertial limit: its continuous time limit is a first order gradient flow with implicit gradient regularization.

#### From the literature

The difference inequality method for the inverse Collatz tree (Krasikov 1989), improved to exponents 0.81 (Applegate and Lagarias 1995) and 0.84 (Krasikov and Lagarias 2003); switched systems (Liberzon 2003); the joint spectral radius (Rota and Strang 1960; Jungers 2009) and its rank one reduction to a maximum cycle mean problem (Ahmadi and Parrilo 2012); the MM reading of gradient descent (Lange, Hunter and Yang 2000); the Lyapunov function of Nesterov's method (Nesterov 2004; Wilson, Recht and Jordan 2021); performance estimation (Drori and Teboulle 2014; Taylor, Hendrickx and Glineur 2017) and the function value contraction of a gradient step (Taylor, Hendrickx and Glineur 2018); modified equations (Hairer, Lubich and Wanner 2006) and implicit gradient regularization (Barrett and Dherin 2021).

#### New results

- [Certified growth exponents for the inverse Collatz tree from a simplified difference inequality method](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#certified_growth_exponents_for_the_inverse_collatz_tree) (Theorem 9.3, page 164; proved): A simplified version of the Krasikov difference inequality method turns lower bounds on how many integers reach a given number into a finite supersolution test over residues modulo a power of 3, and certifies exponents up to 0.477, far below the best known 0.84. New in this book.
- [Counting bound with exponent 0.477 for integers reaching 1](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#simplified_counting_bound_for_integers_reaching_one) (Corollary 9.4, page 165; proved): The simplified method certifies, with a vector found by computer and checked in exact integer arithmetic, that at least x to the power 0.477 integers up to x reach 1, below the exponent 0.84 of Krasikov and Lagarias (2003). New in this book.
- [Switching MM decreases the objective on alternate iterates for every smooth function](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#smm_monotone_on_alternate_iterates) (Proposition 9.5, page 167; proved): Switching MM with step one over L decreases the objective on alternate iterates for every L smooth function, convex or not, with an explicit decrease that yields a bound on the smallest gradient norm. New in this book.
- [Exact joint spectral radius of the descent and injection matrices of Switching MM](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#smm_exact_joint_spectral_radius) (Proposition 9.6, page 168; proved): Because the descent matrix has rank one, the joint spectral radius of the descent and injection matrices of Switching MM is the larger of the spectral radius of the injection matrix and a supremum over a scalar sequence, a variant of a rank one device of Ahmadi and Parrilo (2012). New in this book.
- [Transient bound conjecture for the injection matrix of Switching MM](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#smm_transient_bound_conjecture) (Conjecture 9.7, page 169; open): Conjecture that the transient of repeated injection steps of Switching MM never exceeds the first descent factor, supported by computation on a grid of 200 momentum values and 300 normalized steps. New in this book.
- [Every switching rule between descent and injection is stable on quadratics, conditional on the transient bound](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#every_switching_rule_is_stable_on_quadratics) (Corollary 9.8, page 169; conditional on the transient bound $|\tau_j|<1$ for every $j\ge0$ at the fixed normalized step $a$, where $\tau_j=u^\top N^jv$ is defined in the statement; it is the content of the transient bound conjecture ($|\tau_j|\le1-a$ for all $a\in(0,1]$, $\beta\in[0,1)$ and $j\ge0$), which has been checked numerically on a finite grid of parameters and is not proved): If the transient bound holds, every switching rule between descent and injection steps of Switching MM, including adaptive and state dependent rules, is exponentially stable on a quadratic at step one over L. New in this book.
- [Exact linear rate of Switching MM on smooth strongly convex functions](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#smm_linear_rate_on_smooth_strongly_convex_functions) (Theorem 9.9, page 169; proved): For strongly convex and L smooth functions, two steps of Switching MM at step one over L contract the distance to the minimizer by the product of the classical one step factors of a long and a short gradient step, which explicit functions show is the exact worst case over the class, and the function gap by its square, using the one step function value bound of Taylor, Hendrickx and Glineur (2018). New in this book.
- [Speed of Switching MM relative to gradient descent on smooth strongly convex functions](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#smm_speed_relative_to_gradient_descent) (Corollary 9.10, page 171; proved): For condition numbers above an explicit threshold, the per step rate of Switching MM on the whole class of smooth strongly convex functions has normalized limit two plus beta over two, the slow mode step multiplier of the quadratic analysis, against one for gradient descent. - [Modified equation for period two gradient steps](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#modified_equation_for_period_two_steps) (Proposition 9.11, page 171; proved): To second order, two gradient steps of lengths h1 and h2 follow the gradient flow of the objective plus a multiple of its squared gradient norm, with coefficient one quarter of the mean square step over the mean step; the single step case is the implicit gradient regularization of Barrett and Dherin (2021). chapters.title: Three Point Inequalities and Similar Triangles
chapters.summary:
This chapter asks what the three point inequality for Bregman divergences, the core of convergence proofs for majorization minimization (MM) and accelerated gradient methods, says about Switching MM (the authors' method) and the Collatz map (the 3x+1 problem). It uses relative smoothness, the method of similar triangles and performance estimation. For convex L smooth functions it proves that Switching MM with momentum beta, whose long step 1+beta is at most the golden ratio, has function value error at most L R^2/((2+beta) N) at even N (R the initial distance to a minimizer), and that the 1/J^2 rate in J similar triangles steps survives any switching with plain gradient steps. It conjectures the exact worst case L R^2/((4+2 beta) N+2) at even N for beta up to 0.68614. For the Syracuse map it proves an exact Bregman decomposition of log y_N minus log y_0 into a martingale term (in the stochastic model) and an Itakura Saito dissipation, bounded below by 0.029092 at every odd y at least 3, and explains why the optimality of the step is missing.

#### From the literature

- the three point identity for Bregman divergences (Chen and Teboulle 1993) and the classical three point inequality
- relative smoothness (Bauschke, Bolte and Teboulle 2017; Lu, Freund and Nesterov 2018) and the classical 1/k rate of the MM step
- Nesterov's accelerated method (Nesterov 1983, 2004), the accelerated proximal method (Beck and Teboulle 2009), and the method of similar triangles with its classical energy proof (Gasnikov and Nesterov 2018)
- the exact worst case L R^2/(4N+2) of gradient descent (Drori and Teboulle 2014) and the interpolation conditions behind performance estimation (Taylor, Hendrickx and Glineur 2017)
- long step schedules that beat gradient descent (Grimmer 2024; Altschuler and Parrilo 2025)
- the Itakura Saito divergence as a Bregman divergence (Banerjee, Merugu, Dhillon and Ghosh 2005)

#### New results

Only statements that are the authors' own are catalogued.

- [Convex rate for Switching MM when the long step is at most the golden ratio](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#switching_mm_convex_rate_by_three_point_inequality) (Theorem 10.5, page 179; proved): On smooth convex functions the bound for Switching MM after N steps is L R^2/((2+beta) N), against L R^2/(2N) for gradient descent by the same argument, provided the long step 1+beta is at most the golden ratio, as it is for the book's beta = log_2 3 minus 1. New in this book.
- [Exact convex worst case of Switching MM (conjecture)](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#switching_mm_exact_worst_case_conjecture) (Conjecture 10.6, page 180; open): Conjectured exact worst case L R^2/((4+2 beta) N+2) of Switching MM on smooth convex functions for even N and beta up to about 0.686, supported by performance estimation computations and proved in a later chapter for N = 4, and for N = 2 when beta is at most 0.6446. New in this book.
- [Acceleration by similar triangles survives every switching rule](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#acceleration_survives_every_switching_rule) (Proposition 10.7, page 182; proved): Mixing similar triangles steps with plain gradient steps in any order, even one that depends on the iterates, never increases the energy, so the 1/J^2 rate in the number J of similar triangles steps is kept. New in this book.
- [Bregman decomposition of the logarithmic change along a Syracuse orbit](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#bregman_decomposition_of_a_syracuse_orbit) (Proposition 10.8, page 183; proved): Along any Syracuse orbit the change of the logarithm is exactly a linear term minus a sum of Itakura Saito divergences, and in the stochastic model the linear term is a martingale and the dissipation has mean log(4/3) per step, the size of the drift. New in this book.
- [Uniform lower bound on the Bregman dissipation of the Syracuse map](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#uniform_dissipation_of_the_syracuse_map) (Proposition 10.9, page 185; proved): At every odd y at least 3 the Itakura Saito divergence of the Syracuse multiplier S(y)/y from 1 is at least 0.029092, with equality only at y = 9, and its limit inferior as y grows is 0.037682. New in this book.

chapters.title: Cycles and Continued Fractions
chapters.summary:
This chapter studies the cycle half of the Collatz conjecture (the 3x+1 problem): can the orbit of a positive integer close up into a nontrivial cycle? A cycle with r odd elements and s halvings satisfies the cycle identity, which puts s/r above log_2 3 and bounds the least element through the one sided distance from r log_2 3 up to the next integer. Continued fractions and a mediant lemma give a self contained proof of the classical fact that the first value of r not excluded by a verification range is a best one sided approximation. With Bařina's verification up to 2^68 or 2^71 this gives at least 72,057,431,991 odd elements for every nontrivial cycle, a bound the authors do not claim as new. The chapter also proves Diophantine insufficiency (infinitely many r survive every verification range), a window lemma and what arithmetic information would suffice, and covers an exact integer certificate, negative and rational cycles, Erdős problem 125, Lean 4 and a refined open problem.

#### From the literature

- the cycle identity and the bound on the least element, classical since the 1970s (Böhm and Sontacchi 1978, Steiner 1978)
- the criterion of Crandall (1978) and the bound of at least 17,087,915 elements under the accelerated map of Eliahou (1993)
- the exclusion of m cycles (m ascending runs) for m = 1 (Steiner 1978), up to 68 (Simons and de Weger 2005) and up to 91 (Hercher 2023)
- the length bounds of Hercher (2018), Puchert (2018) and Hercher (2023), the last at least 137,528,045,312 odd elements, conditional on verification to 3·2^69 and so unconditional since Bařina (2025)
- the verification up to 2^68 and 2^71 of Bařina (2021, 2025)
- the optimal criterion of Halbeisen and Hungerbühler (1997) and the rational cycles of Lagarias (1990)
- the classical description of the best one sided approximations by intermediate fractions, stated and proved in Hančl and Turek (2019)
- Erdős problem 125 of Burr, Erdős, Graham and Li (1996), settled by AlphaProof Nexus (Tsoukalas and collaborators 2026)

#### New results

Only statements that are the authors' own are catalogued.

- [Diophantine insufficiency, infinitely many cycle lengths survive any verification range](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#diophantine_insufficiency_cycle_lengths) (Proposition 11.20, page 210; proved): However far the verification of the Collatz conjecture is pushed, infinitely many cycle lengths survive the cycle inequality, so information about the approximation of log2 3 alone cannot exclude all nontrivial cycles, a point Halbeisen and Hungerbühler (1997) made earlier in another form. New in this book.
- [Window lemma, the least element of a cycle lies in an explicit window](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#window_lemma_least_cycle_element) (Lemma 11.21, page 211; proved): Every element of a hypothetical Collatz cycle with m odd steps is at least an explicit lower bound and the least element is below the standard upper bound, so it lies in a window whose endpoints differ by a factor of about m over 3. New in this book.
- [What arithmetic would suffice to exclude all Collatz cycles](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#what_arithmetic_would_suffice) (Corollary 11.22, page 213; conditional on the hypothesis that, for the function $f$ of the statement, every nontrivial cycle of the accelerated map with $m$ odd steps and $k$ steps in all has least element $M<m/(3\Lambda f(m))$, where $\Lambda=k\log2-m\log3$; no such bound is proved in the book): If an argument using the arithmetic of the parity word improved the standard upper bound on the least element of a cycle by a factor slightly above m over 3 for all large m, a finite verification would exclude every nontrivial cycle. New in this book.

chapters.title: The Divergence Half
chapters.summary:
This chapter treats the divergence half of the Collatz conjecture (the 3x+1 problem): can the Syracuse orbit of a positive integer grow without bound? It proves a Cesàro identity linking the logarithmic growth of an orbit to the running mean of the halving exponents (the 2 adic valuations of 3y+1), and deduces that along a divergent orbit this mean has limit superior at most log_2 3, so the lower limit of its fraction of odd steps under the accelerated map is at least 1/log_2 3, about 0.631. The Cesàro liminf conjecture is shown equivalent to the divergence half, and the obvious empirical test is shown to be circular. The model chain on residues modulo 3^a, with independent Geometric(1/2) halving exponents, has a one step law that is the exact limit for random starting values and is exactly stationary after a strides. The chapter also describes Tao's theorem, the Krasikov and Lagarias counting bound, equidistribution along single orbits, and three failed routes (equidistribution, Lyapunov certificates, uniform integrability), and it notes that if the positive density theorems of 2026 described in Chapter 13 hold, convergence to 1 on a set of logarithmic density one would already imply the conjecture.

#### From the literature

- the density theorem of Terras (1976, 1979) and Everett (1977): almost every integer falls below its starting value
- the exponent log 3/log 4 of Korec (1994) for almost every orbit
- the theorem of Tao (2022): almost all orbits attain almost bounded values in logarithmic density, with Syracuse random variables, a fine scale mixing estimate modulo powers of 3, and the identities behind the model chain (loss of memory modulo 3^a, the one step recursion and the stationary law)
- the counting bound of Krasikov and Lagarias (2003): at least x^0.84 integers up to x reach 1
- the branching random walk model of preimages of Lagarias and Weiss (1992)
- the verification up to 2^71 of Bařina (2025)
- the elementary fact, noted many times, that a divergent orbit needs at least a fraction 1/log_2 3 of odd steps

#### New results

Only statements that are the authors' own are catalogued.

- [Cesàro identity for the halving exponents of a Syracuse orbit](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#cesaro_identity) (Proposition 12.3, page 229; proved): Over N strides of the Syracuse map, the logarithmic change of the orbit equals a sum of logarithms minus N times the running mean of the halving exponents times log 2, which ties growth of the orbit to that running mean. New in this book.
- [Cesàro liminf conjecture on the running mean of the halving exponents](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#cesaro_liminf_conjecture) (Conjecture 12.6, page 230; open): Along every Syracuse orbit the lower limit of the running average of the halving exponents is strictly above log2 3, a statement the book shows is equivalent to the divergence half of the Collatz conjecture. New in this book.

chapters.title: Positive Density from the Backward Tree
chapters.summary:
This chapter asks what recent positive density theorems say about the Collatz conjecture (the 3x+1 problem). It presents four unrefereed preprints of 2026 by Mazur, Shaik and Lau, those of Mazur and Lau with Lean formalizations: the integers whose orbit under the Collatz map reaches any target t not divisible by 3 have positive lower density, and a positive proportion of integers n reach 1 within 10.46 log n steps. The proof runs the Syracuse map backwards: it counts predecessors in the inverse tree, weighs backward words by a power of 3 over a power of 2, and uses fine scale mixing of the Syracuse random variable modulo powers of 3. The chapter explains the argument, with Lau's propagation step and the seeds it starts from, and the corollary that upper natural density one for the integers reaching 1 would force every orbit to reach 1. It shows that the forward model of the book is 2 adic and the backward model 3 adic, so that the forward walk of log x and the backward walk of the word weights are one random walk run in two directions. It adds a proposition that, granting the preprints and the verification up to 2^71, a bounded form of Tao's theorem would imply the conjecture. Its computations give the exact backward tree from 1 below 2^24, the step counts below 3 million, the first crossings of random words, and the exact offset law to level 18, where the largest Fourier coefficient stays between 3.6/d^2 and 3.9/d^2 from level 7 on and sits at a power of 2. The book compared the statements with the preprints but has not checked the proofs. It poses problems B1 (bounded Tao), B2 (the mixing rate) and B3 (the sharp rate).

#### From the literature

- the bound of Krasikov and Lagarias (2003): about x^0.84 integers up to x provably reach 1
- the almost bounded values theorem (Tao 2022), with fine scale mixing and Fourier decay of the Syracuse random variable
- the positive lower density theorems of Mazur (2026), with his almost bounded theorem in natural density (2026)
- the step constant 3/log(4/3), about 10.428, of Shaik (2026)
- the explicit constants and Fourier decay of Lau (2026), whose mathematics and Lean formalization were produced by the AxiomProver system
- the propagation of positive density from a seed, Mazur (2026), made explicit by Lau (2026)
- the density one corollary of Mazur (2026, upper density) and Lau (2026, natural density)
- the verification up to 2^71 of Bařina (2025)

#### New results

Only statements that are the authors' own are catalogued, not the theorems of Mazur, Shaik and Lau.

- [A bounded form of Tao's theorem would imply the Collatz conjecture, given the positive density theorems](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#bounded_tao_would_imply_collatz_given_positive_density) (Proposition 13.3, page 247; conditional on the positive density theorem of Mazur (2026) or of Lau (2026), recent unrefereed preprints with Lean formalizations whose proofs the book does not check: for every integer $t\ge1$ not divisible by $3$, the set of positive integers whose orbit under the Collatz map reaches $t$ has positive lower natural density; the computer verification of Bařina (2025) that every positive integer up to $2^{71}$ has an orbit that reaches $1$, which the book cites and does not repeat): If the positive density theorems of Mazur and Lau are right, the Collatz conjecture would follow from a bounded form of Tao's theorem, namely that the least value on the orbit of n is at most 2 to the power 71 for all n in a set of logarithmic density one. chapters.title: The Path to Collatz
chapters.summary:
What would a proof of the Collatz conjecture (the 3x+1 problem) have to contain, and where does each part of the book sit relative to it? The chapter splits the conjecture for the Syracuse map into a divergence half, whether an orbit can be unbounded, equivalent to the Cesàro conjecture on the running mean of the halving exponents relative to log_2 3, and a cycle half, whether a nontrivial cycle exists, governed by the cycle identity and one sided Diophantine approximation of log_2 3. For the divergence half it examines equidistribution modulo powers of 2, Lyapunov certificates of descent and uniform integrability of the iterate martingale, and shows where each fails: statistics over random starting values do not transfer to one orbit, and monotone certificates and optional stopping are blocked. For the cycle half the verified range (2^68, now 2^71) and the semiconvergent ladder of log_2 3 give at least 72,057,431,991 odd elements in a nontrivial cycle, no irrationality measure can close the gap, and the window lemma shows that what is missing is arithmetic information about the parity word, such as whether 2^k minus 3^m can divide c_k. It lists the constants a mechanism must reproduce and the role of Lean verification.

#### From the literature

The split into a divergence half and a cycle half (Lagarias 1985, 2010); the density theorem and uniform distribution of parity vectors of Terras (1976) and Everett (1977); the parity heuristic of Crandall (1978) and the stochastic models of Lagarias and Weiss (1992); the theorem of Tao (2022) on almost bounded values of almost all orbits; the reduction of cycles to Diophantine approximation of log_2 3 by Crandall (1978), Steiner (1978) and Eliahou (1993); best one sided approximations of Hančl and Turek (2019); rational cycles in Halbeisen and Hungerbühler (1997); verification to 2^71 by Bařina (2025); the cycle length record of Hercher (2023).

#### New results

The chapter states no theorem of its own; its Notes credit the proof that Diophantine information cannot exclude all cycles, and the window corollary, to the authors (Chapter 11).

No new results of this chapter are catalogued.

chapters.title: A Computational Path
chapters.summary:
What can computation contribute to a proof of the Collatz conjecture, and does the majorization minimization (MM) reading say where to point it? The chapter separates verification, certificates and evidence. For the cycle half it lays out a five step programme: verification beyond 2^71.88, a Lean proof of the bound of 72,057,431,991 odd elements, a modular sieve on the numbers c_k(w) of the parity word (in runs up to m = 40 and primes below 3000 it excludes 16 shapes, all with m at most 8, of which only eight are not already excluded by size), window sharpening, and a divisibility theorem. For the divergence half it studies residue certificates and the residue sieve, whose uncovered classes grow like 2^(0.95 k), and proves that the exceptional set of 2 adic integers with infinite coefficient stopping time is closed, null and contains one point of each known negative cycle, and that every uncovered class contains infinitely many positive integers, so no finite residue computation closes the divergence half. It discusses the automated termination prover of Yolcu, Aaronson and Heule, reads Lyapunov potentials, the horizon, Switching MM and potentials with memory as constraints on any certificate, and shows why Polyak's heavy ball, gradient dominance and averaging do not transfer to the conjecture.

#### From the literature

chapters.title: Samplers and the Horizon
chapters.summary:
Can simulation, in the form of nested sampling, vertical likelihood Monte Carlo or split sampling, say anything about the Collatz conjecture in polynomial time? The chapter treats the question as rare event simulation: put an energy on the integers, declare the high energy ones interesting, and estimate the prior volume of level sets through the layer cake identity and a weighted slice sampler. The prior is Haar measure on the 2 adic integers and the two energies are the coefficient stopping time and the total stopping time. It proves that level sets of the coefficient stopping time are unions of residue classes of exactly computable volume (Chernoff rate D = 0.0347, hazard staircase, partition function finite exactly for beta up to D), that the total stopping time is almost surely infinite under Haar measure so a finite box is needed, and that a perfect split sampler for the coefficient stopping time, with no inner Markov chain, costs O(K) per draw after an O(K^2) table and reaches residues of prior mass about one in 860 million at depth 400. Beyond the horizon set by bit length, orbits of nearby integers merge, deep level sets are a few trees of merged orbits, and local samplers rarely leave the tree where they start, as a census of total stopping times below 2^26 shows. Simulation cannot decide the conjecture.

#### From the literature

Nested sampling of Skilling (2006); vertical likelihood Monte Carlo and the weighted slice sampler of Polson and Scott (2015); split sampling, with its Rao Blackwellized volume curve and product estimator, of Birge, Chang and Polson (2013); the slice sampler of Neal (2003); the recursive method of uniform generation from counts of Nijenhuis and Wilf (1978), the backward step of the exact sampler; the Terras bijection and density theorem (Terras 1976, Everett 1977); the merging of consecutive integers under the map, called classical in the book, as in Garner (1985) on consecutive integers with the same total stopping time.

#### New results

The perfect sampler is the authors' as a sampler (its backward step is the method of Nijenhuis and Wilf), and so are the two energies proposition, the coalescence heuristic and the tree decomposition.

- [Two energies under Haar measure, the coefficient stopping time and the total stopping time](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#two_energies_coefficient_and_total_stopping_time) (Proposition 16.1, page 281; proved): The level sets of the coefficient stopping time are unions of residue classes with exactly computable volume, while the total stopping time is almost surely infinite under Haar measure, which separates what a sampler can reach from what the conjecture is about. New in this book.
- [Perfect split sampling for the coefficient stopping time](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#perfect_split_sampling_coefficient_stopping_time) (Theorem 16.2, page 282; proved): An exact sampler with no inner Markov chain draws residues whose coefficient stopping time exceeds a given depth, in time linear in the depth after a quadratic table, even when their prior mass is exponentially small. New in this book.
- [Coalescence of orbits shifts the total stopping time](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#orbit_coalescence_shifts_total_stopping_time) (Proposition 16.4, page 285; proved): If the orbits of two positive integers meet at a point other than 1 or 2, their total stopping times differ by exactly the difference of the numbers of steps each takes to reach it. New in this book.

#### Key terms

chapters.title: Progress on the Open Problems
chapters.summary:
This chapter reports progress on problems O4, S2, P3, P4, P5, P7 and P11 of chapter 22, by proof where possible, otherwise by computation. For the Collatz map it studies the cumulants of total stopping times of the accelerated map (O4, P4) and single Syracuse orbits from near 2^100000 and 2^300000 (P3). For Switching MM, the momentum method that alternates a long and a unit gradient step, it treats the exact worst case rate on smooth convex functions (P11) and the noise floor under stochastic gradients (S2, P5). It also extends the exact density of the Erdős 125 sumset A+B to 4^17 (P7). Proved: explicit worst functions bounding the convex rate below for every even N and momentum coefficient below 1; the matching upper bound for N = 2 and 4, by a performance estimation certificate, on ranges containing the Collatz momentum; and the 5/3 noise floor bound, relative to gradient descent, for arbitrary noise covariance on quadratics. Conjectured: the two branch closed form of the convex rate. Numerical evidence only: constant deficits in the cumulants of stopping times (boundedness is open), the 5/3 bound on a logistic regression problem, and no departure from independent sampling along single orbits.

#### From the literature

- the worst case LR^2/(4N+2) of gradient descent on smooth convex functions, by performance estimation (Drori and Teboulle 2014), whose proof structure the chapter follows
- the interpolation conditions for smooth convex functions (Taylor, Hendrickx and Glineur 2017)
- the Huber function, the classical worst case function for gradient descent
- cumulants of first passage times from Wald's identities (Feller 1971, Gut 1988)
- the theorem of Terras (1976), which makes the Bernoulli model exact in the head of an orbit
- Erdős problem 125 (Burr, Erdős, Graham and Li 1996), solved by AlphaProof Nexus (Tsoukalas and others 2026): the lower density of A+B is zero

#### New results

All five labeled statements are the authors' own: one conjecture, one theorem and three propositions, one of them a computed fit.

- [Additive deficits of the second and third cumulants of total stopping times, fitted to the exact census](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#stopping_time_cumulant_deficits_census_fit) (Proposition 17.1, page 296; computed): A fit to the exact census of total stopping times shows that their second and third cumulants grow at the rate of the Bernoulli model up to constant additive deficits, which accounts for the observed skewness; it is a computation on the blocks from 2^20 to 2^30, not a proof for all starting values. New in this book.
- [Conjectured exact worst case rate of Switching MM on smooth convex functions, both branches](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#switching_mm_exact_convex_rate_conjecture) (Conjecture 17.2, page 298; open): A conjectured closed form for the exact worst case of Switching MM on smooth convex functions, for every even number of steps and every momentum coefficient below one, with a main branch and an overshoot branch that cross at an explicit threshold. New in this book.
- [Explicit worst case functions for Switching MM on smooth convex functions](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#switching_mm_explicit_worst_functions) (Proposition 17.3, page 299; proved): Two explicit one dimensional functions, a Huber function and an overshoot function, show that the worst case of Switching MM on smooth convex functions is at least the larger of the two branches of the conjectured exact rate, for every even number of steps and every momentum coefficient below one. New in this book.
- [Exact worst case rate of Switching MM after two and four steps, by an explicit certificate](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#switching_mm_exact_rate_two_and_four_steps) (Theorem 17.4, page 300; proved): For two and four steps and momentum coefficients up to about 0.64 and 0.70, an explicit certificate built from interpolation inequalities proves the conjectured exact rate of Switching MM on smooth convex functions, in ranges that contain the Collatz momentum. New in this book.
- [The five thirds noise floor bound for Switching MM under correlated gradient noise on quadratics](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#switching_mm_noise_bound_correlated_noise) (Proposition 17.5, page 301; proved): On a quadratic with gradient noise of arbitrary covariance, independent from call to call, the stationary excess loss of Switching MM is at most five thirds of that of gradient descent with the same step, for every step up to one over the largest curvature and every momentum coefficient below one. New in this book.

chapters.title: What the Book Missed
chapters.summary:
This chapter asks what the book left unproved within reach on the two halves of the Collatz conjecture, cycles and divergence. For cycles it sharpens the basic inequality on the smallest element of a cycle with r odd elements: the exact cycle identity 3x_0(2^{delta_c}-1) = sum of 2^{W_t} over the walk of halvings (Theorem 18.2) gives the minimum inequality with constant 1/(2 log 2) = 0.7213 in place of 1 (Theorem 18.3, Corollary 18.4), and the positive rational cycles of the Christoffel words attain it (Theorem 18.5), so no inequality in r, s and the minimum alone can do better. A matching bound holds for the largest element (Theorem 18.6, Corollary 18.7). At the record rung r = 72 057 431 991 a rational cycle has minimum above 2^71.41, so excluding integer cycles needs an arithmetic gain of at least 1.33 (Corollary 18.8), and the word of a cycle above 2^71 must stay in a narrow band around the line t log_2 3 (Proposition 18.9), with exact word counts by dynamic programming. For divergence it recasts the Cesàro criterion as a statement about empirical measures on the 2 adic integers (Theorem 18.10) and truncates it to a finite modulus: an orbit is bounded if the odd iterates in classes 1 and 5 modulo 8, with class 5 counted twice, have lower frequency above log_2(3/2) = 0.585 (Proposition 18.11). It also proves an exponential tail in the stride model (Proposition 18.13) and corrects the long run variance on the T_0 clock to (2/27)(log 6)^2 (Proposition 18.14). The open problems M1 to M5 are: records of the sharp ladder bound, branch and bound at q_23, an inequality for integer cycles, counting words with large Phi, and the limsup version of the modulus criterion. Nothing here proves or disproves the conjecture.

#### From the literature

- the minimum inequality with constant 1 (Crandall 1978, Eliahou 1993) and Hercher's Theorem 27 with constant 3/4 (Hercher 2023)
- every periodic parity word is the word of a rational cycle, and the frequency bound for divergent trajectories (Lagarias 1985), whose heuristic count of cycles the chapter sharpens
- balanced words and the study of m cycles (Steiner 1977, Simons and de Weger 2005)
- Koksma's inequality and Ostrowski's discrepancy bound (Kuipers and Niederreiter 1974)
- persistence asymptotics for random walks (Iglehart 1974, Doney 1989), used for the density of large coefficient stopping times (Proposition 18.12, an application of these theorems with a numerical constant, not catalogued)

#### New results

- [The walk of halvings seen from the smallest and the largest element of a cycle](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#walk_of_halvings_seen_from_the_extremes) (Lemma 18.1, page 308; proved): Read from the smallest element of a cycle, the halving count never gets ahead of the line t log_2 3 by more than the closing defect, and read from the largest element it never falls behind that line. New in this book.
- [Exact form of the cycle identity for positive rational cycles](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#exact_form_of_the_cycle_identity) (Theorem 18.2, page 309; proved): For every positive rational cycle and every starting element, three times the element times (2 to the closing defect, minus one) equals the sum of 2 to the walk of halvings over one period, the walk being read from that element. New in this book.
- [Sharp minimum inequality for cycles of the Syracuse map](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#sharp_minimum_inequality) (Theorem 18.3, page 309; proved): The smallest element of a cycle is below a bound that depends only on the number of odd elements and the closing defect, with constant 1/(2 log 2) in place of 1, uniformly in the word. New in this book.
- [The sharp minimum bound on the ladder of rungs and its asymptotics](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#minimum_inequality_on_the_ladder) (Corollary 18.4, page 309; proved): At a rung of the continued fraction ladder of log_2 3 every cycle has its smallest element below G(r), and the sum defining G(r) is r/(2 log 2) up to a lower order term controlled by the partial quotients. New in this book.
- [Christoffel cycles attain the sharp minimum inequality](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#christoffel_cycles_are_extremal) (Theorem 18.5, page 310; proved): The positive rational cycle of the lower Christoffel word of slope s/r has 3 M_w Lambda between 2 to the minus 2 delta times beta_r = r/(2 log 2) + 1/4 + O(1/r) and the sharp bound B_r(delta), and along the rungs the ratio to the sharp bound tends to 1, so no inequality in r, s and the minimum alone can improve the constant 1/(2 log 2). New in this book.
- [Sharp maximum inequality for positive rational cycles](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#sharp_maximum_inequality) (Theorem 18.6, page 311; proved): The largest element of a long cycle is at least about 1/log 2, or 1.4427, times the elementary bound r/(3 Lambda), and the Christoffel cycles attain this. New in this book.
- [Spread of the elements of a long cycle: a factor of about two](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#spread_of_a_long_cycle) (Corollary 18.7, page 312; proved): The largest element of a long cycle at a rung is at least about twice the smallest, and the extremal cycles span exactly that factor. New in this book.
- [Arithmetic gap at the rung r star: a rational cycle above 2 to the 71.41](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#arithmetic_gap_at_the_current_record_rung) (Corollary 18.8, page 313; computed): A positive rational cycle with 72 057 431 991 odd elements has smallest element above 2^71.41, so excluding integer cycles at that size with verification to 2^71 needs a property of integers that improves the sharp minimum inequality by a factor of at least 1.33; the numerical constants come from an exact interval computation of B_r. New in this book.
- [Band: the word of a long cycle stays near the line t log_2 3 for a positive fraction of indices](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#band_for_the_word_of_a_cycle) (Proposition 18.9, page 314; proved): A cycle with large minimum has a positive fraction of indices at which the halving count stays within b of t log_2 3, and at a cycle with r star odd elements and minimum at least 2^71 that fraction is at least 47.6 percent for b = 3. New in this book.
- [Divergence as an invariant measure on the 2 adic integers (reformulation of Lagarias's frequency bound)](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#divergence_as_an_invariant_measure) (Theorem 18.10, page 317; proved): An orbit of a positive integer is unbounded exactly when some, equivalently every, weak limit of its empirical measures gives the odd cylinder mass at least log_3 2; this repackages Lagarias's frequency bound as a statement about invariant measures. New in this book.
- [Finite modulus criterion: a lower frequency bound on classes modulo 2^m forces a bounded orbit](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#finite_modulus_criterion_for_bounded_orbits) (Proposition 18.11, page 317; proved): An orbit is bounded as soon as the odd iterates in the classes 1 and 5 modulo 8, with class 5 counted twice, have lower frequency above log_2(3/2), a bound that equidistribution would exceed with 0.75. New in this book.
- [Exponential tail of the stopping time in the stride model](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#exponential_tail_in_the_stride_model) (Proposition 18.13, page 319; proved): In the stride model with independent geometric halving exponents the probability of not having come down by stride n is at most x^p M(p)^n, a bound that decays exponentially at rate 0.0550 per stride at the best exponent. New in this book.
- [Long run variance of the log path on the T_0 clock, correcting the factor one third remark](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#variance_on_the_t0_clock) (Proposition 18.14, page 319; proved): In the renewal model the long run variance per step of the log path on the clock of T_0 is (2/27)(log 6)^2, about 0.2378, and the dispersion of the total stopping time grows like 269.7 log n; this corrects an earlier remark of the book. New in this book.
- [Problem M1: records of the sharp ladder bound occur only at rungs](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#records_of_the_ladder_problem) (Problem M1, page 321; open): Prove that the records of the sharp bound B_r(delta(r))/(3 log 2 delta(r)) occur only at the rungs of the ladder, as is proved for the elementary bound F. New in this book.
- [Problem M2: branch and bound exclusion of cycles at r = q_23](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#branch_and_bound_at_q23_problem) (Problem M2, page 321; open): Implement a branch and bound search over cycle words read from the minimum and find the smallest verification range at which it excludes cycles with 137 528 045 312 odd elements. New in this book.
- [Problem M3: an inequality for integer cycles that fails for some rational cycle](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#integer_cycle_inequality_problem) (Problem M3, page 321; open): Find, without computer search, an inequality valid for integer cycles but false for some rational cycle that improves the sharp minimum inequality by a constant factor at all large rungs. New in this book.
- [Problem M4: counting admissible words with large Phi](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#words_with_large_phi_problem) (Problem M4, page 322; open): Count the admissible cycle words with Phi at least c times B_r, for c between 0.75 and 1, and prove that the exponential rate of this count exists and compute it. New in this book.
- [Problem M5: the limsup version of the finite modulus criterion](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#limsup_version_problem) (Problem M5, page 322; open): Prove that along every Syracuse orbit the limsup of f_1 + 2 f_5 exceeds log_2(3/2), a weaker statement than the liminf criterion that would still imply that no orbit is unbounded. New in this book.

#### Key terms
