chapters.title: The Price of a Quantifier
chapters.summary:
This chapter reads a seventeen state, two symbol Turing machine that beeps infinitely often if and only if the Collatz conjecture is true (Theorem 19.1, from the Mira Cult repository, 2026) as a statement about the logical shape of the problem. The conjecture is a Pi_2 sentence of arithmetic and the weak conjecture, no nontrivial cycles, is Pi_1; the difference is one quantifier, which costs three states over Reams's fourteen state weak Collatz machine, a heavy tail in the running time, and an a priori bound on the stopping time in any proof in Peano arithmetic. Proved: a computable bound S on the total stopping time turns the conjecture into a Pi_1 sentence, equivalent to the non halting of an ordinary Turing machine and to the unsolvability of one Diophantine equation (Theorem 19.2). The machine's clock is quadratic in the value, and in the Bernoulli model with factors 1/2 and 3/2 the clock scaled by n squared has a tail of index one half, infinite mean and a tight family (Theorem 19.3, by optional stopping and a change of measure, with the Kesten and Goldie perpetuity as a remark); no function above half the square of the value is a supermartingale (Proposition 19.5). Computed: records of the total stopping time to 10^6, an empirical tail index of 0.513 for the deterministic clock, and an independent simulator that agrees with the macro rules in 96 000 configurations and in 2 times 10^8 transitions from the blank tape. The open problems Q1 to Q5 ask for minimality of seventeen states, a halting machine under a stopping time bound, constants for the clock, deterministic excursion densities and binary encodings.

#### From the literature

- the seventeen state beeping machine equivalent to the full Collatz conjecture, with its macro rules and closed form running times (Mira Cult repository, 2026; listed on the Busy Beaver wiki as not independently verified, and checked by simulation in Section 19.6 of the chapter)
- the weak Collatz conjecture in BB(14) (Reams 2026, verified by Ligocki), Collatz like rules in small Busy Beaver machines (Michel 1993, Aaronson 2020), and the cryptid list of the Busy Beaver wiki
- the MRDP theorem (Matiyasevich 1993), Kreisel's theorem on provably total functions in the form of Fairtlough and Wainer (1998), and Conway's undecidability of generalized Collatz maps (1972)
- the branching random walk prediction of the stopping time constant 41.6776 (Lagarias and Weiss 1992)
- the cycle identity and its Diophantine bounds (Steiner 1977, Simons and de Weger 2005)
- the implicit renewal theorem for perpetuities (Kesten 1973, Goldie 1991), used in a remark of the chapter

#### New results

- [A computable bound on the total stopping time makes the Collatz conjecture a Pi_1 sentence](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#collapse_of_a_computable_stopping_time_bound) (Theorem 19.2, page 327; proved): Assuming a computable bound S on the total stopping time turns the Collatz conjecture into a Pi_1 sentence, equivalent to the non halting of an ordinary Turing machine and to the unsolvability of one Diophantine equation, and the sentence implies the conjecture. New in this book.
- [Tail of the quadratic clock in the Bernoulli model: index one half, infinite mean, tight](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#tail_of_the_clock_in_the_bernoulli_model) (Theorem 19.3, page 330; proved): In the Bernoulli model the quadratic clock of the machine, scaled by n squared, has a tail of index one half with explicit lower constant, so its mean is infinite for every n at least 2 while the scaled family is tight. New in this book.
- [No supermartingale majorizes half the square in the Bernoulli model](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#no_supermartingale_majorant_of_the_clock) (Proposition 19.5, page 332; proved): In the Bernoulli model no nonnegative function above half the square of the value is a supermartingale from some start, so a Lyapunov function bounding the clock's per step cost cannot decrease in expectation. New in this book.
- [Problem Q1: is seventeen states minimal for a beeping machine equivalent to the full Collatz conjecture](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#minimality_of_seventeen_states_problem) (Problem Q1, page 333; open): Decide whether seventeen states is minimal for a beeping machine equivalent to the full Collatz conjecture; the authors conjecture that the three state difference from the weak conjecture is close to the price of the Pi_2 quantifier in this encoding. New in this book.
- [Problem Q2: a halting machine under the stopping time conjecture](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#halting_machine_under_the_stopping_time_conjecture_problem) (Problem Q2, page 333; open): Give an explicit formally proved BB(m) machine that halts exactly when the stopping time bound with a logarithmic budget fails, by adding a budget to the arithmetic core. New in this book.
- [Problem Q3: explicit constants and the deterministic tail of the clock](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#explicit_constants_for_the_clock_problem) (Problem Q3, page 333; open): Give explicit constants in the tail theorem and the perpetuity constant, and decide whether the deterministic clock has the same tail and whether the empirical index 0.513 converges to one half. New in this book.
- [Problem Q4: a deterministic density version of the excursion bound](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#deterministic_excursion_density_problem) (Problem Q4, page 333; open): Prove that the set of n up to N whose maximal excursion is at least K n has size at most C N over K, and decide whether it follows from the methods of the backward tree chapter. New in this book.
- [Problem Q5: the state count at which the clock turns logarithmic](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#binary_encodings_problem) (Problem Q5, page 333; open): Find the state count at which a binary encoding changes the clock from quadratic to logarithmic per step, and decide whether the tail of the clock then becomes light. New in this book.

chapters.title: Ratchets, Records and Tails
chapters.summary:
This chapter, added after the first edition, applies the methods of the book to Conway's generalized Collatz maps and takes up Problems M1, M4, B1 and B2. Nothing in it proves the conjecture; it sharpens what a proof must do. On the subclass of Conway maps whose multipliers are coprime to the modulus, the digit bijection, the Lyapunov function, the martingale bound and density one descent hold with full proofs, while Conway's theorem and an unprovability proposition show that no method covers the whole class. The equipartition argument is the entropy dual of the Lyapunov argument and gives the same exponent, the entropy deficit 0.05004 bits per step. Two Conway maps with bounded orbits can alternate to a map with divergent orbits (a deterministic Parrondo pair); measure preservation forbids this for a common modulus, and with two moduli the Collatz map is one of two losing games that win together. For cycles, the sharp minimum inequality is an equality for the Christoffel cycle at every rung, Problem M1 is false as stated and true in its exact form (records occur only at rungs), and for Problem M4 there are exact counts, a rigorous Chernoff upper bound and a supermultiplicative lower bound. Granting Lau's theorem (an unrefereed preprint), the conjecture is equivalent to a polynomial bound on the tail of the orbit minimum, where Tao's theorem gives a logarithmic one. For Problem B2 a Feynman and Kac recursion computes single Fourier coefficients of the Syracuse variable to level 2000, and the largest decays like n^(-3/2) 3^(-0.05004 n), conjectured and not proved; the Switching MM viewpoint and an experiment on basins of 3x+d maps (one cycle in 312 455 captures 3.7 percent of starting values) close the chapter, followed by open problems R1 to R14. The chapter credits Halbeisen and Hungerbuhler (1997) with the exact minimum bound and the concatenation identity.

#### From the literature

- Conway's theorem that multiplicative generalized Collatz maps compute every partial recursive function (Conway 1972)
- the theorem of Tao (2022) on almost bounded values in logarithmic density, and the positive density theorems of Mazur (2026) and Lau (2026), unrefereed, on which the tail criterion depends
- Parrondo's paradox of two losing games that win together, in its deterministic form here
- the largest minimal element of a rational cycle with given length and number of odd steps, with the concatenation identity (Halbeisen and Hungerbuhler 1997), of which the chapter's exact minimum bound is the same statement in other notation
- Christoffel words and the mechanical word of a given intercept; a recent preprint on Christoffel words as extremal structures in the same setting (2026), not compared line by line
- Sanov and Chernoff large deviation rates, and Cramer type moderate deviations

#### New results

- [Digit bijection for coprime Conway maps](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#digit_bijection_of_coprime_conway_maps) (Theorem 20.4, page 337; proved): For a coprime Conway map the first k digits of x modulo d^k are a bijection onto digit strings, so on a complete residue system they are independent and uniform. New in this book.
- [Lyapunov and martingale structure of coprime Conway maps](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#lyapunov_and_martingale_structure_of_coprime_conway_maps) (Theorem 20.5, page 338; proved): Under Haar measure the multiplier moments of a coprime Conway map give a family of martingales, drift negative exactly when the product of multipliers is below d^d, a maximal inequality with exponent theta star, and a uniform bound on the probability that the multiplier reaches 1. New in this book.
- [Density one descent for coprime Conway maps of negative drift](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#density_one_descent_for_coprime_conway_maps) (Theorem 20.6, page 339; proved): For a coprime Conway map with negative drift the integers with an iterate smaller than themselves within k steps have lower density at least one minus rho_min to the k, so almost every integer descends. New in this book.
- [A Conway map whose descent no sound theory proves](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#unprovable_descent_for_a_conway_map) (Proposition 20.7, page 340; proved): For any sound recursively axiomatized theory there is a Conway map all of whose orbits reach 1 but for which the theory does not prove this, so it has no Lyapunov function provable in the theory. New in this book.
- [Entropy and Lyapunov duality for coprime Conway maps](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#entropy_and_lyapunov_duality) (Theorem 20.8, page 340; proved): The minimal relative entropy of digit laws with nonnegative log drift equals minus log base 2 of rho_min, and counts the digit strings of length k with multiplier at least 1 as 2 to the k times (log_2 d minus eta) up to o(k). New in this book.
- [A deterministic Parrondo pair of Conway maps](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#deterministic_parrondo_pair) (Theorem 20.9, page 342; proved): Two modulus four Conway maps each of whose orbits reaches a cycle or fixed point have an alternation whose every orbit tends to infinity, with C(n)=9n+4 for even n. New in this book.
- [No ratchet under measure preservation](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#no_ratchet_under_measure_preservation) (Theorem 20.10, page 343; proved): Under Haar measure the expected logarithmic multiplier of any composition of p copies of one coprime Conway map and q of another is p mu_A plus q mu_B, so two maps of negative drift cannot be combined into one of positive drift. New in this book.

- [Exact bound on the smallest element of a rational cycle, attained by the Christoffel cycle](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#exact_minimum_bound_for_rational_cycles) (Theorem 20.12, page 347; proved): Every positive rational cycle satisfies 3M(2^delta minus 1) at most B prime r of delta, with equality exactly for the mechanical word, and at a rung the maximal minimum over cycles is attained by the Christoffel cycle alone. The maximal minimum and its attainment by the mechanical word are due to Halbeisen and Hungerbuhler (1997); the characterization of equality for every closing defect is stated here. New in this book.
- [Concatenation identity for the first elements of rational cycles](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#concatenation_of_rational_cycles) (Lemma 20.14, page 348; proved): For words with positive closing defects the first element of the concatenated cycle is a weighted mean of the first elements with explicit positive weights, and Phi is additive with a twist. Halbeisen and Hungerbuhler (1997) give the same identity. New in this book.
- [Additivity of the closing defect below the next rung](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#additivity_of_defects_below_the_next_rung) (Lemma 20.15, page 348; proved): Between a rung q and the next rung the closing defect of r is the sum of those of q and r minus q, and partial sums of defects stay below 1. New in this book.
- [Records of the exact bound occur only at rungs](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#records_of_the_exact_bound_occur_at_rungs) (Theorem 20.16, page 348; proved): For r not a rung the mechanical word is that of u followed by that of q, the exact bound at r is a weighted mean of those at u and q, and so a new record of the bound can occur only at a rung. New in this book.
- [The record statement M1 as stated fails](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#statement_m1_as_stated_fails) (Proposition 20.17, page 349; proved): The ratio R(2q)/R(q) exceeds 1 for rungs q at least 2 with 2q below the next rung, so records of R occur at non rungs such as 10, 15, 82, 612 and 918. New in this book.
- [Chernoff bound at every rung for words with large Phi](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#chernoff_upper_bound_at_every_rung) (Proposition 20.18, page 350; proved): The count of admissible words with Phi at least c B_r is bounded by a minimum over lambda of a matrix product partition function, with explicit nonnegative matrices indexed by depth. - [Supermultiplicativity of the counts of words with large Phi](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#supermultiplicativity_of_the_word_counts) (Proposition 20.19, page 350; proved): Between rungs the count of words with large Phi satisfies N*(c,r) at least N*(c,u) N*(c,q), so the count at jq is at least the j th power of the count at q. - [A polynomial tail bounds the least counterexample](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#polynomial_tail_bounds_the_least_counterexample) (Corollary 20.21, page 352; conditional on Lau's theorem (Theorem 13.1, from an unrefereed preprint), that for every t prime to 3 the integers whose orbit reaches t have lower natural density at least t^(-4)/D_A, which the book does not prove): Granting Lau's theorem, a bound K C^(-4-epsilon) on the tail of the orbit minimum bounds any least counterexample explicitly, so the conjecture reduces to a finite computation. - [Cramer regime for the logarithmic multiplier of coprime Conway maps](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#cramer_regime_for_coprime_conway_maps) (Proposition 20.25, page 354; proved): For a coprime Conway map with unequal multipliers and n uniform modulo d^k, the upper tail of the logarithmic multiplier has the Gaussian asymptotic with the Mills ratio factor for deviations x_k tending to infinity with x_k=o(k^(1/6)). - [Feynman and Kac recursion for the Fourier coefficients of the Syracuse variable](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#feynman_kac_recursion_for_fourier_coefficients) (Proposition 20.26, page 354; proved): The Fourier coefficient u_n(B) of the Syracuse variable at the frequency 2^B satisfies an explicit recursion from level n-1 to level n, which with a truncated window of exponents computes the table to level n in O(n^2) operations. chapters.title: Contributions and a Computational Road Map
chapters.summary:
What does the book establish about the Collatz conjecture (the 3x+1 problem), which proof strategies does it rule out, and what computational road map remains? The chapter does not prove the conjecture. It collects the book's contributions in a table, a ledger of obstructions listing each strategy shown to fail and what survives it, and four corrections. Its organizing idea is the integrality principle: an argument that uses only a bounded number of binary digits of the starting value holds unchanged on the 2 adic integers, where the map has a fixed point and further cycles, so it cannot prove the conjecture. The road map has a shared kernel and two lanes: a cycle lane that ends at a gate needing a divisibility theorem about 2^k minus 3^m and c_k(w), and a divergence lane that searches a string rewriting formulation for a termination certificate, which would settle both halves but may not exist. One further route goes through density: given the unrefereed positive density preprints of Mazur and Lau presented in Chapter 13, a bounded form of Tao's theorem (problem B1) would also settle the whole conjecture.

#### From the literature

The theorem of Tao (2022) that almost every orbit attains almost bounded values in logarithmic density; the counting exponent 0.84 of Krasikov and Lagarias (2003); verification up to 2^71 (Bařina 2025); the cycle length bound from the continued fraction of log_2 3 (Eliahou 1993, sharpened by Hercher 2023); the exclusion of cycles with m ascending runs (Simons and de Weger 2005 for small m, Hercher 2023 up to m = 91); least denominator fractions in an interval (Hercher 2023) and the best one sided approximations (Hančl and Turek 2019); the equivalence of the conjecture with termination of a string rewriting system, and the matrix interpretation search (Yolcu, Aaronson and Heule 2023); the undecidability theorem of Conway (1972); the integrality principle as folklore of the 2 adic literature (Lagarias 1985); the unrefereed positive density preprints of Mazur (2026) and Lau (2026).

#### New results

The chapter collects the book's contributions and states no new theorem; its table points to the chapters that state and credit each result.

No new results of this chapter are catalogued.

chapters.title: Open Problems and Computational Projects
chapters.summary:
Which questions does the book leave open, and which finite computations are worth doing? The chapter restates the open problems of the book in their sharpest form, for the divergence half of the Collatz conjecture (O1 Cesàro equidistribution, O2 trajectory mixing modulo powers of 3, O3 and O3' certificates with growing horizon and potentials of unbounded depth, O4 the third cumulant of total stopping times and the variance deficit, O5 uniform integrability, which is settled), for the cycle half (C1 an arithmetic sharpening of the cycle identity, C2 effective irrationality measures for log_2 3, C3 sharper accountings at the next rungs of the ladder), for the backward tree of the positive density theorems (B1 a bounded form of Tao's theorem, B2 the true mixing rate of the 3 adic offset law, B3 the sharpness of the threshold 3/log(4/3)), and for Switching MM (S1 rates beyond quadratics and S3 the best period two ratio, both partly settled, S2 stochastic analysis, S4 adaptive switching). It says what is known for each, points to the progress reported in Chapter 17, and flags formulations that turn out to be wrong. It then lists eleven computational projects, P1 to P11, each with a success criterion: a machine checked cycle bound in Lean 4, thresholds and the window lemma, orbits from very large starting values, total stopping time cumulants at scale, Switching MM against Nesterov, heavy ball and Adam, periodic schedules, Erdős 125 beyond 4^13, perfect samplers beyond the coefficient stopping time, trees of slow integers, a pilot for the divergence lane of Chapter 21, and the exact convex rate of Switching MM. The unnumbered Gallery of Orbits that follows shows seven computed plates.

#### From the literature

Questions going back to Terras (1976), Steiner (1978) and Eliahou (1993), restated as O1, O3, C2 and the cycle formulation; the fine scale mixing results of Tao (2022) behind O2; the explicit irrationality measure of log_2 3 of Rhin (1987); the cycle length record of Hercher (2023) and the verification to 2^71 of Bařina (2025); the note of Polson and Sokolov (2026) on the AlphaProof Nexus system of Tsoukalas and others (2026), the source of C1 and of the Erdős 125 analogy; the positive density preprints of Mazur, Shaik and Lau (2026) behind B1 to B3; the terminating rewriting systems of Yolcu, Aaronson and Heule (2023) behind P10; the performance estimation of Drori and Teboulle (2014) behind P11; in the gallery, the density bound of Hasler and Melfi (2024) and the branching random walk model of Lagarias and Weiss (1992).

#### New results

This chapter poses problems and projects and proves no theorem of its own.

- [Trajectory mixing of Syracuse residues modulo powers of 3](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#trajectory_mixing_of_syracuse_residues) (Problem O2, page 377; open): Asks for a proof that, from a random starting value, the residues modulo a power of 3 along a Syracuse orbit are distributed as in the random model of the book, whose Markov chain mixes exactly; numerically, modulo 243, they approach the model law at the rate of independent sampling. New in this book.
- [Failure fraction of Lyapunov potentials of growing depth for the Syracuse map](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#failure_fraction_of_potentials_of_growing_depth) (Problem O3$'$, page 378; open): Asks how small the fraction of odd integers at which a Lyapunov potential fails can be made when the potential may read further ahead along the orbit, and whether it can be driven to zero; the answer is a question about the random model of the book, not about the arithmetic of the map. New in this book.
- [Boundedness of the variance deficit and the third cumulant of total stopping times](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#bounded_variance_deficit_of_total_stopping_times) (Problem O4, page 378; open): Asks for a proof that the shortfall of the variance of total stopping times against the random model, which an exact census finds to be an additive and apparently bounded term concentrated in the final descent of the orbit, stays bounded as the starting values grow, and for an explanation of their skewness, which is smaller than the model predicts. New in this book.
- [Arithmetic sharpening of the window bound on the least element of a Collatz cycle](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#arithmetic_sharpening_of_the_cycle_window) (Problem C1, page 379; open): Asks for an improvement, drawn from the arithmetic of the parity vector, of the bound on the least element of a hypothetical Collatz cycle; a strong enough improvement would reduce the cycle half of the conjecture to a finite computation. First stated in Polson and Sokolov (2026), Five Bayesian problems raised by AlphaProof Nexus, manuscript.
- [Verification ranges that exclude the later rungs under Hercher's sharper accounting](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#verification_ranges_for_later_rungs_under_hercher_accounting) (Problem C3, page 380; open): Asks for the computation that would extend Hercher's computer assisted exclusion of Collatz cycles of a given length to the next lengths in line, the rungs of the one sided continued fraction ladder of log2 3. New in this book.
- [Bounded form of Tao's theorem: orbit minimum at most 2^71 on a set of logarithmic density one](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#bounded_form_of_tao_theorem) (Problem B1, page 380; open): Asks for a proof that the least value on the orbit of n is at most 2 to the power 71 for all n in a set of logarithmic density one, a bounded form of Tao's theorem that, given the positive density theorems of Mazur and Lau, would imply the Collatz conjecture, and which the conjecture implies. New in this book.
- [True decay rate of the Fourier coefficients of the Syracuse random variable modulo powers of 3](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#true_decay_rate_of_syracuse_fourier_coefficients) (Problem B2, page 380; open): Asks how fast the largest Fourier coefficient of the Syracuse random variable modulo 3 to the power d, over frequencies prime to 3, tends to zero, choosing between decay like exp of minus c times the square of log d, like exp of minus c times d to a power gamma below 1, and eventually geometric decay. New in this book.
- [Sharpness of Shaik's threshold 3/log(4/3) for total stopping times](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#sharpness_of_shaik_threshold_for_stopping_times) (Problem B3, page 381; open): Asks for a proof that, for every constant c below 3 over log(4/3), the integers n whose total stopping time is at most c log n have natural density zero, so that the threshold of Shaik for positive density is sharp. New in this book.
- [Exact worst case function gap rate of Switching MM for small condition numbers](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#exact_function_gap_rate_of_switching_mm_for_small_condition_numbers) (Problem S1, page 381; open): The worst case rate of Switching MM is known exactly for the distance to the minimizer, and for the function gap on ill conditioned problems; the problem asks for the exact function gap rate, and the function that attains it, on well conditioned problems, where numerical performance estimation shows that the known bound is not tight. New in this book.
- [Five thirds noise bound of Switching MM beyond quadratics](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#five_thirds_noise_bound_of_switching_mm_beyond_quadratics) (Problem S2, page 381; open): Asks to extend the proven robustness of Switching MM to gradient noise, a stationary error at most five thirds of that of gradient descent for every momentum coefficient below one, from quadratic objectives to all smooth strongly convex objectives. New in this book.
- [A principled adaptive switching rule for Switching MM](https://vsokolov.org/books/collatz/results.html#adaptive_switching_rule_for_switching_mm) (Problem S4, page 382; open): Asks for a rule, using only the smoothness constant and observed function values, that decides when Switching MM injects momentum, keeping its proven robustness to gradient noise while matching the speed of momentum applied at every step on noiseless problems. New in this book.

chapters.title: Numerical Constants

Reference table of the numerical constants of the book, to six significant figures unless stated otherwise, all recomputed with the book's scripts: the drift log(sqrt(3)/2) and the step variance of the accelerated map, the model drift and variance per stride of the Syracuse map, total stopping time slopes in the model and observed, the central limit constant, the Chernoff rate D of the density theorem, the residue sieve exponent h, the Cesàro threshold log_2 3, the Switching MM momentum beta = log_2 3 minus 1 with its noise amplification, effective step multiplier and stability limit, and the parity autocorrelations of the model. chapters.title: Code
chapters.summary:
Where the code of the book is. Every number computed in the book was produced by a short Python script, and numbers quoted from the literature are cited where they appear. The scripts use mpmath, NumPy, SciPy, SymPy and Matplotlib, with Numba for the census of total stopping times and for the gallery, CVXPY with the Clarabel solver for performance estimation, and scikit-learn only to load one data set; they run in seconds to minutes on a laptop and are in the folder book/scripts of the public repository, released under the MIT License. The appendix lists two scripts in full. The first computes the partial quotients of log_2 3, builds the candidate rungs of the semiconvergent ladder, keeps the records of the one sided distance and returns the first rung not excluded by a verified range, which by the one sided ladder theorem of Chapter 11 and the mediant lemma is the exact cycle bound. The second derives symbolically the slow mode noise amplification factor of Switching MM. An index lists all other scripts by chapter, including the script that writes the table of total stopping times below 2^26 that most scripts of Chapter 16 read.

The script reproduces the cycle bound of Eliahou (1993) at verified range 2^40; its bound at 2^68 is unchanged at the range 2^71 of Bařina (2025).

results.name: Martingale structure of the renewal model for the standard Collatz map
results.summary: In the renewal model of the standard Collatz map, where every tripling is followed by a halving, the iterates are not a martingale, but they become one once each coming tripling is booked in advance.
results.statement: Let $(B_n)_{n\ge0}$ be the Markov chain on $\{0,1\}$ with $\mathbb{P}(B_{n+1}=0\mid B_n=1)=1$ and $\mathbb{P}(B_{n+1}=0\mid B_n=0)=\mathbb{P}(B_{n+1}=1\mid B_n=0)=\tfrac12$, let $x_0>0$, and put $x_{n+1}=3x_n$ if $B_n=1$ and $x_{n+1}=x_n/2$ if $B_n=0$, with $\mathcal{F}_n=\sigma(B_0,\ldots,B_n)$ (the renewal model for the standard Collatz map, which sends an even $m$ to $m/2$ and an odd $m$ to $3m+1$, where $B_n$ models the parity of the $n$th iterate). Write $\delta^{*}=\log(\sqrt3/2)$. Then (i) the stationary law of the chain satisfies $\mathbb{P}(B_n=1)=\tfrac13$, and the fraction of odd steps (indices $i$ with $B_i=1$) among the first $n$ steps converges to $\tfrac13$ almost surely from any initial state; (ii) $(x_n)$ is not a martingale, since $\mathbb{E}[x_{n+1}\mid\mathcal{F}_n]=3x_n$ on $\{B_n=1\}$, but $M_n=3^{B_n}x_n$ is a martingale; (iii) $(\log x_n)$ is not a supermartingale, since its increment is $+\log3$ on $\{B_n=1\}$, but $\log M_n$ is a supermartingale with conditional drift $0$ on $\{B_n=1\}$ and $\delta^{*}$ on $\{B_n=0\}$; (iv) almost surely $\frac1n\log x_n\to\tfrac13\log3 - \tfrac23\log2=\tfrac13\log\tfrac34=\tfrac23\delta^{*}\approx -0.0959$; (v) if $\tau_1<\tau_2<\cdots$ are the successive times at which $B_n=1$, then $X_j=x_{\tau_j}$ satisfies $X_{j+1}=3X_j2^{-K_{j+1}}$, where $K_{j+1}=\tau_{j+1} - \tau_j - 1$ are independent with the Geometric$(\tfrac12)$ law $\mathbb{P}(K=k)=2^{-k}$ for $k\ge1$, and $(X_j)$ is a martingale because $\mathbb{E}[3\cdot2^{-K}]=3\sum_{k\ge1}4^{-k}=1$.
results.label: prop:ch3:standard

results.name: Exact parity autocorrelation function of the renewal model for the standard Collatz map
results.summary: In the renewal model of the standard Collatz map one step in three is odd and the parity autocorrelation at lag h is minus one half raised to the power h.
results.statement: Let $(B_n)_{n\ge0}$ be the Markov chain on $\{0,1\}$ with $\mathbb{P}(B_{n+1}=0\mid B_n=1)=1$ and $\mathbb{P}(B_{n+1}=0\mid B_n=0)=\mathbb{P}(B_{n+1}=1\mid B_n=0)=\tfrac12$ (the renewal model for the standard Collatz map, where $B_n$ models the parity of the $n$th iterate), started from its stationary law. Then $(B_n)$ is stationary with $\mathbb{P}(B_n=1)=\frac{1}{1+\mathbb{E}[K]}=\frac13$ and $\operatorname{Var}(B_n)=\frac29$, where $K$, the number of zeros between successive ones of the chain, has the Geometric$(\tfrac12)$ law $\mathbb{P}(K=k)=2^{-k}$ for $k\ge1$ (so $\mathbb{E}[K]=2$), and its autocorrelation function is $\rho(h)=\operatorname{Corr}(B_n,B_{n+h})=\bigl(-\tfrac12\bigr)^{h}$ for $h\ge0$.
results.label: thm:autocorr

results.name: Long run variance of the log path in the renewal model for the standard Collatz map
results.summary: The negative parity correlations of the renewal model cut the long run variance of the log path to one third of its value for independent parities with the same frequency, one in three, of odd steps.
results.statement: Let $(B_n)_{n\ge0}$ be the Markov chain on $\{0,1\}$ with $\mathbb{P}(B_{n+1}=0\mid B_n=1)=1$ and $\mathbb{P}(B_{n+1}=0\mid B_n=0)=\mathbb{P}(B_{n+1}=1\mid B_n=0)=\tfrac12$, started from any initial state, let $x_0>0$, and put $x_{n+1}=3x_n$ if $B_n=1$ and $x_{n+1}=x_n/2$ if $B_n=0$ (the renewal model for the standard Collatz map). Let $\rho(h)=(-\tfrac12)^h$ be the autocorrelation function of $(B_n)$. The autocorrelation factor is $\mathcal{A}:=1+2\sum_{h\ge1}\rho(h)=1+2\cdot\frac{-1/2}{1+1/2}=\frac13$, and the variance of the log path satisfies $\frac{\operatorname{Var}(\log x_n)}{n}\longrightarrow\mathcal{A}\cdot\frac29(\log6)^2=\frac{2}{27}(\log6)^2\approx0.2378$ as $n\to\infty$.
results.label: cor:longrun

results.name: The stopped martingale of the Bernoulli model is not uniformly integrable
results.summary: The martingale of the Bernoulli model, stopped when the iterate first drops to 1 or below, is not uniformly integrable, because the unabsorbed paths keep expected value at least the starting value minus 1 while their probability tends to zero.
results.statement: Let $x_0>1$ and let $\xi_1,\xi_2,\ldots$ be independent random variables with $\mathbb{P}(\xi_i=\tfrac12)=\mathbb{P}(\xi_i=\tfrac32)=\tfrac12$, and put $x_n=x_0\xi_1\cdots\xi_n$ (the Bernoulli model for the accelerated Collatz map) and $\tau=\inf\{n\ge0:x_n\le1\}$. Then $\tau<\infty$ almost surely, the stopped process $(x_{n\wedge\tau})_{n\ge0}$ is a nonnegative martingale converging almost surely to $x_\tau\le1$, and it is not uniformly integrable. More precisely, for every $n$, $\mathbb{E}\bigl[x_n\mathbf{1}_{\{\tau>n\}}\bigr]\ge x_0 - 1$, while $\mathbb{P}(\tau>n)\to0$ as $n\to\infty$.
results.label: prop:uimartingale

results.name: Passage time of the stride model with overshoot
results.summary: In the random stride model of the Collatz map, the expected number of strides for log x to fall to zero or below is the starting log x plus the mean overshoot, which lies between log 2 and 2 log 2, divided by log(4/3), the size of the drift.
results.statement: Consider the stride model of the Collatz map. Let $K_1,K_2,\dots$ be independent random variables with $\mathbb{P}(K_j=k)=2^{-k}$ for $k\ge1$ (the Geometric$(\tfrac12)$ law), fix $x_0>1$, and put $x_j=x_{j-1}\cdot3\cdot2^{-K_j}$, so that $\log x_j=\log x_0+\Delta_1+\dots+\Delta_j$ with $\Delta_j=\log3-K_j\log2$. Let $\tau$ be the first $j$ with $\log x_j\le0$, and let $O=-\log x_\tau\ge0$ be the overshoot below $0$ at time $\tau$. Then $\log2\le\mathbb{E}[O]<2\log2$ and \[\frac{\log x_0+\log2}{|\log(3/4)|}\le\mathbb{E}_{x_0}[\tau]<\frac{\log x_0+2\log2}{|\log(3/4)|}.\]
results.label: prop:ch4:passage

results.name: Stride descent theorem for the Syracuse map
results.summary: One Syracuse stride lowers log x exactly when the halving exponent is at least 2 and raises it exactly when x is 3 mod 4, with sharp bounds on the size of the change.
results.statement: Let $S$ be the Syracuse map on the odd positive integers, $S(x)=(3x+1)/2^{k}$ with $k=v_2(3x+1)$, where $v_2(m)$ is the exponent of the largest power of $2$ dividing $m$. Let $x\ge3$ be odd and $k=v_2(3x+1)$. (i) $\log S(x)-\log x=\log(3+1/x)-k\log2$. (ii) If $k\ge2$, then $S(x)<x$, $\log S(x)-\log x\le\log\bigl(\tfrac34+\tfrac1{4x}\bigr)<0$, and $\log S(x)-\log x\le\log(7/9)$, with equality exactly at $x=9$. (iii) If $k=1$, which happens exactly when $x\equiv3\pmod4$, then $S(x)=(3x+1)/2>x$ and $\log\tfrac32<\log S(x)-\log x=\log\bigl(\tfrac32+\tfrac1{2x}\bigr)\le\log\tfrac53$, with equality on the right exactly at $x=3$.
results.label: thm:stride

results.name: No monotone strong Lyapunov function for a single Syracuse stride
results.summary: No strictly increasing function of x is a strict or strong Lyapunov function for the Syracuse map, because every integer congruent to 3 mod 4, half of all odd integers, ascends in one stride.
results.statement: Let $S$ be the Syracuse map on the odd positive integers, $S(x)=(3x+1)/2^{v_2(3x+1)}$, where $v_2(m)$ is the exponent of the largest power of $2$ dividing $m$. Let $W$ be a strictly increasing function from the odd positive integers to $(0,\infty)$, and let $\rho\le1$. Then $W(S(x))>\rho\,W(x)$ for every $x\equiv3\pmod4$. In particular no strictly increasing $W$ is a strict Lyapunov function for $(S,\{1\})$ (one with $W(S(x))<W(x)$ for every odd $x\ne1$) or a strong Lyapunov function for $(S,\{1\})$ (one with $W>0$ and $W(S(x))\le\rho W(x)$ for every odd $x\ne1$, for some constant $\rho<1$), and the set of odd integers on which $W(S(x))\le\rho W(x)$ fails contains the residue class $3\bmod4$, which has natural density $\tfrac12$ among the odd integers; for $\rho=1$ the set on which it fails is exactly this class.
results.label: thm:nolyapunov

results.name: Exact behaviour of two Syracuse strides
results.summary: Over two Syracuse strides an odd integer decreases exactly when the two halving exponents sum to at least 4, which holds for half of the odd integers, and the largest two stride ascent is log(17/7), attained only at 7.
results.statement: Let $S$ be the Syracuse map on the odd positive integers, $S(x)=(3x+1)/2^{v_2(3x+1)}$, where $v_2(m)$ is the exponent of the largest power of $2$ dividing $m$. For odd $x$ write $k_1=v_2(3x+1)$, $k_2=v_2(3S(x)+1)$ and $S^{(2)}(x)=S(S(x))$. Let $x\ge3$ be odd. (i) $S^{(2)}(x)<x$ if and only if $k_1+k_2\ge4$. (ii) The odd integers with a two stride descent, that is with $S^{(2)}(x)<x$, have natural density exactly $\tfrac12$ among the odd integers. (iii) $\max_{x\ge3\text{ odd}}\bigl(\log S^{(2)}(x)-\log x\bigr)=\log\tfrac{17}{7}\approx0.8873$, attained only at $x=7$, where $S(7)=11$ and $S^{(2)}(7)=17$.
results.label: prop:ch4:twostride

results.name: No fixed horizon monotone certificate for Collatz descent
results.summary: For every fixed number J of strides, no strictly increasing function of x certifies descent over J Syracuse strides, because the odd integers congruent to minus 1 modulo 2 to the J+1 ascend for J strides in a row.
results.statement: Let $S$ be the Syracuse map on the odd positive integers, $S(x)=(3x+1)/2^{v_2(3x+1)}$, where $v_2(m)$ is the exponent of the largest power of $2$ dividing $m$, and let $S^{(J)}$ be its $J$th iterate. Fix $J\ge1$, $\rho\le1$ and a strictly increasing function $W$ from the odd positive integers to $(0,\infty)$. Then $W(S^{(J)}(x))>\rho\,W(x)$ for every odd $x\equiv-1\pmod{2^{J+1}}$, that is, for every $x=2^{J+1}q-1$ with $q\ge1$. This set is infinite and has natural density $2^{-J}$ among the odd integers. Moreover, along it, \[\frac{S^{(J)}(x)}{x}\longrightarrow\Bigl(\frac32\Bigr)^{J}\qquad(q\to\infty).\]
results.label: cor:ch4:multistride

results.name: The linear majorizer of log cannot certify Collatz descent
results.summary: In the stochastic model the tangent line majorizer of log x has a positive mean increment per step of the standard map while log x has a negative one, so the linear surrogate cannot certify descent.
results.statement: Let $T_0$ be the standard Collatz map, $T_0(x)=x/2$ for even $x$ and $T_0(x)=3x+1$ for odd $x$, and let $g(y\mid x)=\log x+(y-x)/x$ be the tangent line majorizer of $\log$ at $x$, so that the surrogate increment $g(T_0(x)\mid x)-g(x\mid x)$ equals $-\tfrac12$ for even $x$ and $2+1/x$ for odd $x$. Under the stochastic model for the standard map, in which the parities of successive steps form a stationary renewal chain $(B_n)$ on $\{0,1\}$ (with $B_n=1$ for an odd step; an odd step is always followed by an even step, and an even step is followed by an odd or an even step with probability $\tfrac12$ each), so that a step is odd with stationary probability $\tfrac13$, the mean surrogate increment per step of $T_0$ is $\tfrac13\cdot2+\tfrac23\cdot\bigl(-\tfrac12\bigr)=+\tfrac13>0$, up to the $O(1/x)$ term, whereas the mean true increment per step is $\tfrac13\log3-\tfrac23\log2=\tfrac13\log(3/4)\approx-0.0959<0$. Per Syracuse stride, that is one odd step followed by $k$ even steps, in the stride model with $k$ distributed as Geometric$(\tfrac12)$ on $\{1,2,\dots\}$, the per step surrogate increments summed over the stride, with the majorizer recentred at every step, have mean $+1$ up to the $O(1/x)$ term, and the mean true increment is $\log(3/4)\approx-0.2877$.
results.label: prop:mmfails

results.name: Power majorizers of log and the Wald root of the stride model
results.summary: In the stride model the power majorizers of log with exponent strictly between 0 and 1 have strictly negative mean increment, interpolating between the true drift log(3/4) and the zero drift of the linear majorizer at the Wald root 1.
results.statement: Work in the stride model of the Collatz map, in which the log increment of one stride is $\Delta=\log3-K\log2$ with $K$ distributed as Geometric$(\tfrac12)$ on $\{1,2,\dots\}$, and write $M(p)=\mathbb{E}[e^{p\Delta}]=3^{p}/(2^{1+p}-1)$. For $0<p\le1$ let $g_p(y\mid x)=\log x+\frac{(y/x)^{p}-1}{p}$; each $g_p$ dominates $\log y$ and is tangent to it at $y=x$, and $p=1$ is the tangent line (linear) majorizer of $\log$. Then the mean stride increment of the surrogate $g_p$, ignoring the $1/x$ correction, is $(M(p)-1)/p$, and: (i) $M(0)=M(1)=1$, and $M(p)<1$ for $0<p<1$; (ii) $p\mapsto(M(p)-1)/p$ is increasing on $(0,1]$, tends to $\mathbb{E}[\Delta]=\log(3/4)$ as $p\downarrow0$, and equals $0$ at $p=1$. In particular every power majorizer with $0<p<1$ has strictly negative mean surrogate increment, and the linear majorizer $p=1$ sits exactly on the boundary.
results.label: prop:ch4:power

results.name: No residue potential for the Collatz map at any modulus
results.summary: No potential made of log x plus a function of residues modulo a power of 2 decreases at every step of the accelerated Collatz map for all large x, because the residue graph has cycles of positive weight, such as the loop at minus 1.
results.statement: Let $T$ be the accelerated Collatz map, $T(x)=x/2$ for even $x$ and $T(x)=(3x+1)/2$ for odd $x$. Fix $d\ge1$ and let $G_d$ be the directed graph on the residues modulo $2^d$ in which the residue $a$ has an edge to each residue $a'$ with $a'\equiv T(a)\pmod{2^{d-1}}$ (the two lifts of $T(a)$), with weight $w(a)=\log(3/2)$ if $a$ is odd and $w(a)=-\log2$ if $a$ is even. (i) There are a function $\varphi$ on $\mathbb{Z}/2^d\mathbb{Z}$ and a bound $X$ such that $V(T(x))<V(x)$ for all integers $x\ge X$, where $V(x)=\log x+\varphi(x\bmod2^d)$, if and only if every cycle of $G_d$ has negative total weight. (ii) For every $d\ge1$ the graph $G_d$ contains cycles of positive weight: the loop at $-1$, of weight $\log(3/2)$, and the images of the cycles of $T$ on the negative integers, whose weights are $r\log3-s\log2>0$ for a cycle with $r$ odd steps among $s$ steps. The maximum cycle mean of $G_d$ is exactly $\log(3/2)$ for every $d$. (iii) Consequently no potential $\log x+\varphi(x\bmod2^d)$ with bounded $\varphi$ decreases at every step for all large $x$, for any $d$, and the same holds for potentials required to decrease over any fixed number $J$ of steps.
results.label: thm:ch5c:residue

results.name: Surplus of a pointwise potential along runs of trailing ones
results.summary: A potential log x plus a correction that decreases at every Syracuse stride needs an unbounded correction, with a surplus growing linearly in the number of trailing ones of x.
results.statement: Let $S$ be the Syracuse map on the odd positive integers, $S(x)=(3x+1)/2^{v_2(3x+1)}$, where $v_2(m)$ is the exponent of the largest power of $2$ dividing $m$, and let $V(x)=\log x+\varphi(x)$ for a real function $\varphi$ on the odd positive integers. Suppose $V(S(x))<V(x)$ for every odd $x\ge3$. Then for every $j\ge2$ and every odd $q\ge1$, \[\varphi(2^jq-1)-\varphi(2\cdot3^{j-1}q-1)\;>\;(j-1)\log\frac32 .\] In particular $\varphi$ is unbounded above or below, and $\sup\varphi-\inf\varphi\ge(j-1)\log(3/2)$ for every $j$.
results.label: prop:ch5c:surplus

results.name: Run length potential and its failure fraction
results.summary: With weight c above log(3/2), the run length potential log x plus c times the 2 adic valuation of x+1 decreases at all but finitely many ascending strides, but under the stride model it fails to decrease at a positive fraction of odd integers, 0.2087 at weight c equal to 1.
results.statement: Let $S$ be the Syracuse map on the odd positive integers, $S(x)=(3x+1)/2^{k}$ with $k=v_2(3x+1)$, where $v_2(m)$ is the exponent of the largest power of $2$ dividing $m$, let $\varepsilon(x)=\log\bigl(1+\tfrac1{3x}\bigr)$, and for $c>\log(3/2)$ let $V_c(x)=\log x+c\,v_2(x+1)$. Then $V_c$ decreases at every ascending stride (a stride with $k=1$) from an odd $x>1/\bigl(2(e^c-3/2)\bigr)$, hence at every ascending stride when $c>\log(5/3)$ and at all but finitely many when $c\le\log(5/3)$. The descending strides ($k\ge2$) at which $V_c$ fails to decrease are exactly those $x\mapsto y=S(x)$, with $k$ halvings, that land on a $y$ with $v_2(y+1)-1\ge(k\log2-\log3-\varepsilon(x))/c$. Under the stride model, in which $k$ and $v_2(y+1)$ are independent Geometric$(\tfrac12)$ variables on $\{1,2,\dots\}$, the fraction of odd $x$ at which $V_c$ fails to decrease is \[p(c)=\sum_{k\ge2}2^{-k}\,2^{-\lceil(k\log2-\log3)/c\rceil},\] which is $0.2087$ at $c=1$ and decreases to $0.1431$ as $c\downarrow\log(3/2)$, and $V_c$ fails at a positive fraction of odd integers for every $c$.
results.label: prop:ch5c:runpot

results.name: The extrapolated point of Switching MM is a long gradient step
results.summary: For every differentiable objective, two consecutive steps of Switching MM from an even index are exactly a long gradient step, longer by the factor one plus the momentum coefficient, followed by a plain gradient step.
results.statement:
Let $f:\mathbb{R}^d	o\mathbb{R}$ be differentiable, let $\alpha>0$, and write $G_h(x)=x-h
abla f(x)$ for a gradient step of length $h$. Switching MM with step $\alpha$ and momentum coefficient $ eta$ starts from $x_{-1}=x_0$, takes the plain gradient step $x_{t+1}=G_\alpha(x_t)$ at even $t$, and at odd $t$ takes the extrapolated step $x_{t+1}=G_\alpha(y_t)$ with $y_t=x_t+ eta(x_t-x_{t-1})$. Let $t$ be even. Then $x_{t+1}=G_\alpha(x_t)$, and the extrapolated point at the following odd iteration is $y_{t+1}=x_{t+1}+ eta(x_{t+1}-x_t)=x_t-(1+ eta)\alpha
abla f(x_t)=G_{(1+ eta)\alpha}(x_t)$. Consequently $x_{t+2}=G_\alpha igl(G_{(1+ eta)\alpha}(x_t) igr)$, and in the form that exhibits the momentum, $x_{t+2}=x_{t+1}- eta\alpha

results.label: lem:ch6:ystep

results.name: Two step equivalence of Switching MM with cyclic gradient steps on quadratics
results.summary: On a strongly convex quadratic, two steps of Switching MM from an even index equal a plain gradient step followed by a longer one, so the method is a cyclic step size method and every two steps its error is multiplied by an explicit degree two polynomial of the Hessian.
results.statement:
Let $f(x)=	frac12x^	op Ax-b^	op x$ with $A$ symmetric positive definite and minimizer $x^\ast=A^{-1}b$, let $\alpha>0$ and $ eta\ge0$, write $G_h(x)=x-h
abla f(x)$, and let $(x_t)$ be generated by Switching MM with step $\alpha$ and momentum coefficient $ eta$ (it starts from $x_{-1}=x_0$, takes the plain gradient step $x_{t+1}=x_t-\alpha
abla f(x_t)$ at even $t$, and at odd $t$ takes the extrapolated step $x_{t+1}=y_t-\alpha
abla f(y_t)$ with $y_t=x_t+ eta(x_t-x_{t-1})$). For every even $t\ge0$, $x_{t+2}=G_{(1+ eta)\alpha}(x_{t+1})=G_{(1+ eta)\alpha} igl(G_\alpha(x_t) igr)$, that is, two steps of Switching MM from an even index are a gradient step of length $\alpha$ followed by a gradient step of length $(1+ eta)\alpha$, and every iterate of Switching MM is an iterate of this cyclic schedule. In terms of the error $e_t=x_t-x^\ast$, $e_{t+2}=(I-\alpha A) igl(I-(1+ eta)\alpha A igr)e_t$ for even $t$.
results.label: thm:smmquad

results.name: Stability range and linear convergence of Switching MM on quadratics
results.summary: Switching MM converges linearly on every strongly convex quadratic for any momentum coefficient below one and step at most one over L, and it is stable exactly for normalized steps below an explicit limit.
results.statement: Let $f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Ax-b^\top x$ with $A$ symmetric positive definite whose largest eigenvalue is $L$, let $\alpha>0$ and $0\le\beta<1$, and let Switching MM with step $\alpha$ and momentum coefficient $\beta$ (it starts from $x_{-1}=x_0$, takes the plain gradient step $x_{t+1}=x_t-\alpha\nabla f(x_t)$ at even $t$, and at odd $t$ takes the extrapolated step $x_{t+1}=y_t-\alpha\nabla f(y_t)$ with $y_t=x_t+\beta(x_t-x_{t-1})$) have the two step multiplier $\rho(a)=(1-a)\bigl(1-(1+\beta)a\bigr)=1-(2+\beta)a+(1+\beta)a^2$ on an eigendirection with eigenvalue $\lambda$ and normalized step $a=\alpha\lambda$. Then for real $a$, $|\rho(a)|<1$ if and only if $0<a<(2+\beta)/(1+\beta)$. In particular Switching MM converges linearly on every strongly convex quadratic whenever $\alpha\le1/L$, and in fact whenever $\alpha L<(2+\beta)/(1+\beta)$. For all $a>0$, $\rho(a)\ge1-(2+\beta)^2/\bigl(4(1+\beta)\bigr)$, a minimum attained at $a=(2+\beta)/\bigl(2(1+\beta)\bigr)$.
results.label: cor:ch6:stability

results.name: Slow mode effective step of Switching MM on quadratics
results.summary: In the slow directions Switching MM behaves like gradient descent with a step enlarged by the factor two plus beta over two, about 1.29 at the Collatz momentum, so it is not an accelerated method.
results.statement: Let $f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Ax-b^\top x$ with $A$ symmetric positive definite, let $\alpha>0$ and $\beta\ge0$, and let Switching MM with step $\alpha$ and momentum coefficient $\beta$ (it starts from $x_{-1}=x_0$, takes the plain gradient step $x_{t+1}=x_t-\alpha\nabla f(x_t)$ at even $t$, and at odd $t$ takes the extrapolated step $x_{t+1}=y_t-\alpha\nabla f(y_t)$ with $y_t=x_t+\beta(x_t-x_{t-1})$) have the two step multiplier $\rho(a)=(1-a)\bigl(1-(1+\beta)a\bigr)$ on an eigendirection with eigenvalue $\lambda$ and normalized step $a=\alpha\lambda$ (that is, the error component along that eigenvector satisfies $e_{t+2}=\rho(a)e_t$ for even $t$). As $a\to0$, $\rho(a)=1-(2+\beta)a+O(a^2)$, and the per step contraction factor $|\rho(a)|^{1/2}$ equals $1-\tfrac{2+\beta}{2}a+O(a^2)$. Thus in the slow directions Switching MM behaves like gradient descent with the effective step $m_{\mathrm{SMM}}\,\alpha$, where $m_{\mathrm{SMM}}=\tfrac{2+\beta}{2}$, which is $1.2925$ at $\beta=\log_23-1$.
results.label: cor:ch6:slow

results.name: Third order defect of the cyclic step representation of Switching MM
results.summary: For objectives with a Lipschitz Hessian, the failure of the odd iterates of Switching MM to follow a cyclic gradient path is of third order in the step size, and it vanishes for quadratics.

abla f(x)$, and let $(x_t)$ be generated by Switching MM with step $\alpha$ and momentum coefficient $ eta$ (it starts from $x_{-1}=x_0$, takes the plain gradient step $x_{t+1}=x_t-\alpha
abla f(x_t)$ at even $t$, and at odd $t$ takes the extrapolated step $x_{t+1}=y_t-\alpha
abla f(y_t)$ with $y_t=x_t+ eta(x_t-x_{t-1})$). For even $t$, with $h=x_{t+1}-x_t=-\alpha
abla f(x_t)$, $x_{t+2}-G_{(1+ eta)\alpha}(x_{t+1})=\alpha igl[(1+ eta)
abla f(x_{t+1})- eta
abla f(x_{t+1}-h)-
abla f(x_{t+1}+ eta h) igr]$, and $ igl\|x_{t+2}-G_{(1+ eta)\alpha}(x_{t+1}) igr\|\le	frac{M}{2}\, eta(1+ eta)\,\alpha^3\,\|
