results.name: Problem Q4: a deterministic density version of the excursion bound
results.summary: Prove that the set of n up to N whose maximal excursion is at least K n has size at most C N over K, and decide whether it follows from the methods of the backward tree chapter.
results.statement: The excursion bound of the Bernoulli model is a statement about the model. Is there a deterministic density version, that the set of $n\le N$ with $t(n)\ge Ln$ has size at most $CN/L$, and does it follow from the methods of the chapter on the backward tree?
results.label: prob:ch21:excursions

results.name: Problem Q5: the state count at which the clock turns logarithmic
results.summary: Find the state count at which a binary encoding changes the clock from quadratic to logarithmic per step, and decide whether the tail of the clock then becomes light.
results.statement: A binary encoding of the value would make the clock $O(\log v)$ per step at the cost of many more states. Where is the state count at which the clock changes from quadratic to logarithmic, and does the tail of the clock then become light?
results.label: prob:ch21:binary

results.name: Digit bijection for coprime Conway maps
results.summary: For a coprime Conway map the first k digits of x modulo d^k are a bijection onto digit strings, so on a complete residue system they are independent and uniform.
results.statement: Let $T$ be a coprime Conway map. For every $k\ge 1$ the map \[ x \bmod d^k \;\longmapsto\; (x_0,x_1,\dots,x_{k-1}) \] is a well defined bijection from $\mathbb{Z}/d^k\mathbb{Z}$ onto $\{0,\dots,d-1\}^k$. Hence if $x$ is uniform on a complete residue system modulo $d^k$, its first $k$ digits are independent and uniform on $\{0,\dots,d-1\}$.
results.label: rrt:thm:bijection

results.name: Lyapunov and martingale structure of coprime Conway maps
results.summary: Under Haar measure the multiplier moments of a coprime Conway map give a family of martingales, drift negative exactly when the product of multipliers is below d^d, a maximal inequality with exponent theta star, and a uniform bound on the probability that the multiplier reaches 1.
results.statement: Let $T$ be a coprime Conway map and let $x$ be Haar distributed on $\mathbb{Z}_d$, or uniform modulo $d^k$. \begin{enumerate} \item[(a)] $\mathbb{E}\,[M_k^\theta]=\rho(\theta)^k$ for every real $\theta$, and $M_k^\theta/\rho(\theta)^k$ is a martingale in $k$. \item[(b)] $\Lambda$ is convex with $\Lambda(0)=0$ and $\Lambda'(0)=\mu$. There is $\theta>0$ with $\rho(\theta)<1$ if and only if $\mu<0$, that is, if and only if $\prod_i m_i<d^{\,d}$. \item[(c)] If $\mu<0$ and some $m_i>d$, there is a unique $\theta^*>0$ with $\rho(\theta^*)=1$, the process $M_k^{\theta^*}$ is a martingale, and \[ \mathbb{P}\Big(\sup_{k\ge 0} M_k \ge u\Big)\le u^{-\theta^*}\qquad (u\ge 1). \] \item[(d)] For every $k$, $\;\mathbb{P}(M_k\ge 1)\le \rho_{\min}^{\,k}$, where $\rho_{\min}=\min_{\theta\ge 0}\rho(\theta)$. \end{enumerate}
results.label: rrt:thm:lyap

results.name: Density one descent for coprime Conway maps of negative drift
results.summary: For a coprime Conway map with negative drift the integers with an iterate smaller than themselves within k steps have lower density at least one minus rho_min to the k, so almost every integer descends.
results.statement: Let $T$ be a coprime Conway map with $\mu<0$. For each $k$, the set of positive integers $n$ with $|T^j(n)|<n$ for some $j\le k$ has lower density at least $1-\rho_{\min}^{\,k}$. In particular almost every positive integer, in the sense of natural density, has an iterate smaller than itself.
results.label: rrt:thm:density

results.name: A Conway map whose descent no sound theory proves
results.summary: For any sound recursively axiomatized theory there is a Conway map all of whose orbits reach 1 but for which the theory does not prove this, so it has no Lyapunov function provable in the theory.
results.statement: Let $\mathcal{T}$ be any sound, recursively axiomatized theory, for example ZFC if it is sound. There is a Conway map $g$ all of whose orbits reach $1$ such that $\mathcal{T}$ does not prove this. In particular $g$ admits no Lyapunov function whose descent property is provable in $\mathcal{T}$.
results.label: rrt:prop:unprovable

results.name: Entropy and Lyapunov duality for coprime Conway maps
results.summary: The minimal relative entropy of digit laws with nonnegative log drift equals minus log base 2 of rho_min, and counts the digit strings of length k with multiplier at least 1 as 2 to the k times (log_2 d minus eta) up to o(k).
results.statement: Let $T$ be a coprime Conway map with $\mu<0$ and let $u$ be the uniform law on digits. Then \[ \eta\;:=\;\min\Big\{D(q\,\|\,u)\;:\;\sum_i q_i\log\frac{m_i}{d}\ge 0\Big\}\;=\;-\log_2\rho_{\min} , \] where $D$ is relative entropy in bits. The number of digit strings of length $k$ with $M_k\ge 1$ is $2^{k(\log_2 d-\eta)+o(k)}$.
results.label: rrt:thm:duality

results.name: A deterministic Parrondo pair of Conway maps
results.summary: Two modulus four Conway maps each of whose orbits reaches a cycle or fixed point have an alternation whose every orbit tends to infinity, with C(n)=9n+4 for even n.
results.statement: Define two Conway maps with modulus four on the nonnegative integers by \[ A(n)=\begin{cases}3n+1 & n \text{ even}\\ \lfloor n/4\rfloor & n \text{ odd,}\end{cases} \qquad B(n)=\begin{cases}3n+1 & n \text{ odd}\\ \lfloor n/4\rfloor & n \text{ even.}\end{cases} \] \begin{enumerate} \item[(a)] Every orbit of $A$ enters the cycle $\{0,1\}$. \item[(b)] Every orbit of $B$ enters the fixed point $\{0\}$ or the cycle $\{1,4\}$. \item[(c)] Every orbit of the alternation $C=B\circ A$ tends to infinity, and $C(n)=9n+4$ for all even $n$. \end{enumerate}
results.label: rrt:thm:parrondo

results.name: No ratchet under measure preservation
results.summary: Under Haar measure the expected logarithmic multiplier of any composition of p copies of one coprime Conway map and q of another is p mu_A plus q mu_B, so two maps of negative drift cannot be combined into one of positive drift.
results.statement: Let $T_A$ and $T_B$ be coprime Conway maps with the same modulus $d$ and drifts $\mu_A,\mu_B$. Under Haar measure on $\mathbb{Z}_d$, the expected logarithmic multiplier of any composition of $p$ copies of $T_A$ and $q$ copies of $T_B$, in any order, equals $p\,\mu_A+q\,\mu_B$. In particular two maps with negative drift cannot be combined into one with positive drift.
results.label: rrt:thm:noparrondo

results.name: Collatz as game A: a resonant pair with positive drift
results.summary: Both the Collatz map and a modulus three map lose, but their alternation has an invariant Haar measure, i.i.d. round multipliers and positive drift for every m at least 7, and almost every integer has a larger iterate.
results.statement: Let $T$ be the Collatz map, let $B=B_m$ as above and let $C=B\circ T$. \begin{enumerate} \item[(a)] Both games lose: $\mu_T=\tfrac12\log\tfrac34<0$ and $\mu_B=\tfrac13\log\tfrac{m}{27}<0$, and by Theorem 20.6 almost every positive integer has a smaller iterate under $T$ and under $B$. \item[(b)] Haar measure on $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_3$ is invariant under $C$. Under it the multipliers of successive rounds are independent and identically distributed, equal to \[ \frac{m}{2}\ \text{ w.p. } \tfrac12,\qquad \frac16\ \text{ w.p. } \tfrac13,\qquad \frac{m}{6}\ \text{ w.p. } \tfrac16 . \] \item[(c)] The drift of a round is \[ \mu_C=\mu_T+\tfrac12\log\frac{m}{3}+\tfrac12\mu_B=\frac16\log\frac{m^4}{1728}, \] which is positive for every $m\ge 7$. The naive value $\mu_T+\mu_B$ is negative. \item[(d)] The first $k$ rounds of $n$ depend only on $n \bmod 6^k$, and the set of positive integers $n$ with $|C^j(n)|>n$ for some $j\le k$ has lower density at least $1-\rho_C^{\,k}$, where $\rho_C=\min_{\theta\ge 0}\mathbb{E}\,[M^{-\theta}]<1$ and $M$ is the round multiplier of (b). In particular almost every positive integer has a larger iterate under $C$. \end{enumerate}
results.label: rrt:thm:resonance

results.name: Exact bound on the smallest element of a rational cycle, attained by the Christoffel cycle
results.summary: Every positive rational cycle satisfies 3M(2^delta minus 1) at most B prime r of delta, with equality exactly for the mechanical word, and at a rung the maximal minimum over cycles is attained by the Christoffel cycle alone. The maximal minimum and its attainment by the mechanical word are due to Halbeisen and Hungerbuhler (1997); the characterization of equality for every closing defect is stated here.
results.statement: Every positive rational cycle with $r$ odd elements, closing defect $\delta_c$ and smallest element $M$ satisfies \[ 3M\,(2^{\delta_c}-1)\le B'_r(\delta_c), \] with equality if and only if the word read from $M$ is the mechanical word of intercept $\delta_c$. At a rung $r$ with $s=\lceil r\theta\rceil$ one has $B'_r(\delta(r))=B_r=\sum_{t<r}2^{-\{t\theta\}}$, the mechanical word is the lower Christoffel word of slope $s/r$, its first element is its smallest, and therefore \[ \max\{M\}=M_{\mathrm{Chr}}=\frac{B_r}{3\,(2^{\delta(r)}-1)}, \] the maximum being over all positive rational cycles with these $r$ and $s$, attained by the Christoffel cycle alone.
results.label: rrt:thm:exact

results.name: Concatenation identity for the first elements of rational cycles
results.summary: For words with positive closing defects the first element of the concatenated cycle is a weighted mean of the first elements with explicit positive weights, and Phi is additive with a twist. Halbeisen and Hungerbuhler (1997) give the same identity.
results.statement: Let $w_1,w_2$ be words with closing defects $\delta_1,\delta_2>0$. Then $\Phi(w_1w_2)=\Phi(w_1)+2^{\delta_1}\Phi(w_2)$, and the first elements of the three rational cycles satisfy \[ x_0(w_1w_2)=\frac{(2^{\delta_1}-1)\,x_0(w_1)+2^{\delta_1}(2^{\delta_2}-1)\,x_0(w_2)}{2^{\delta_1+\delta_2}-1}, \] a weighted mean with positive weights. In particular $x_0(w^j)=x_0(w)$.
results.label: rrt:lem:concat

results.name: Additivity of the closing defect below the next rung
results.summary: Between a rung q and the next rung the closing defect of r is the sum of those of q and r minus q, and partial sums of defects stay below 1.
results.statement: Let $q$ be a rung, $q^+$ the next rung, and $q<r<q^+$. Put $u=r-q$. Then $\delta(r)=\delta(q)+\delta(u)$, and $\delta(v)+\delta(q)<1$ for every $1\le v\le u$.
results.label: rrt:lem:add

results.name: Records of the exact bound occur only at rungs
results.summary: For r not a rung the mechanical word is that of u followed by that of q, the exact bound at r is a weighted mean of those at u and q, and so a new record of the bound can occur only at a rung.
results.statement: Let $r$ be a positive integer that is not a rung, $q$ the largest rung below $r$ and $u=r-q$. Then the mechanical word of $r$ is the mechanical word of $u$ followed by the mechanical word of $q$, and \begin{align*} G^*(r)&=\frac{(2^{\delta(u)}-1)\,G^*(u)+2^{\delta(u)}(2^{\delta(q)}-1)\,G^*(q)}{2^{\delta(r)}-1}\\ &\le\max\{G^*(u),G^*(q)\}. \end{align*} Consequently $G^*(r)>\max_{r'<r}G^*(r')$ only if $r$ is a rung. Moreover $G^*(jq)=G^*(q)$ whenever $jq<q^+$.
results.label: rrt:thm:records

results.name: The record statement M1 as stated fails
results.summary: The ratio R(2q)/R(q) exceeds 1 for rungs q at least 2 with 2q below the next rung, so records of R occur at non rungs such as 10, 15, 82, 612 and 918.
results.statement: Let $R(r)=B_r(\delta(r))/(3\log 2\,\delta(r))$ with the capped sum $B_r(\delta)$ of Theorem 18.3. If $q\ge 2$ is a rung with $2q<q^+$ then \[ \frac{R(2q)}{R(q)}=1+\frac{(2^{\delta(q)}-1)(B_q-1)}{2B_q}>1 . \] In particular $R(10)=25.692>R(5)=25.189=\max_{r<10}R(r)$, and $10$ is not a rung. Below $20000$ the records of $R$ that are not rungs are $10$, $15$, $82$, $612$ and $918$, all multiples of the rungs $5$, $41$ and $306$.
results.label: rrt:prop:false

results.name: Chernoff bound at every rung for words with large Phi
results.summary: The count of admissible words with Phi at least c B_r is bounded by a minimum over lambda of a matrix product partition function, with explicit nonnegative matrices indexed by depth.
results.statement: For $\lambda\ge0$ let $Z_r(\lambda)=\sum_w e^{\lambda\Phi(w)}$ over admissible words. Then \[ \frac1r\log_{10}N(c,r)\le\min_{\lambda\ge0}\frac{\log Z_r(\lambda)-\lambda\,c\,B_r}{r\log 10}, \] and $Z_r(\lambda)$ is the product of $r$ nonnegative matrices indexed by depth, with entries $e^{\lambda2^{-\{t\theta\}-j}}$ for $j'\le j+g_t-1$ and $0$ otherwise.
results.label: rrt:prop:chernoff

results.name: Supermultiplicativity of the counts of words with large Phi
results.summary: Between rungs the count of words with large Phi satisfies N*(c,r) at least N*(c,u) N*(c,q), so the count at jq is at least the j th power of the count at q.
results.statement: Let $N^*(c,r)$ count the words of length $r$ with $K_t\le\lfloor t\theta+\delta(r)\rfloor$, $K_r=\lceil r\theta\rceil$ and $\Phi(w)\ge c\,B'_r(\delta(r))$; at a rung $N^*=N$. If $r$ is not a rung, $q$ is the largest rung below it and $u=r-q$, then \[ N^*(c,r)\ge N^*(c,u)\,N^*(c,q), \] and in particular $N^*(c,jq)\ge N(c,q)^j$ for $jq<q^+$.
results.label: rrt:prop:super

results.name: Tail criterion: the conjecture is equivalent to a polynomial tail bound on the orbit minimum
results.status_text: conditional on Lau's theorem (Theorem 13.1, from an unrefereed preprint), that for every t prime to 3 the integers whose orbit reaches t have lower natural density at least t^(-4)/D_A, which the book does not prove
results.conditions: Lau's theorem (Theorem 13.1, from an unrefereed preprint), that for every t prime to 3 the integers whose orbit reaches t have lower natural density at least t^(-4)/D_A, which the book does not prove.
results.summary: Granting Lau's theorem, a least counterexample m star forces the tail E(C) of the orbit minimum to be at least 1/(16 m_star^4 D_A), so the conjecture is equivalent to a tail bound of that form for C at least 2^71.
results.statement: Assume Lau's theorem. If the Collatz conjecture fails, let $m_*$ be the least positive integer whose orbit does not reach $1$. Then \[ E(C)\ \ge\ \frac{1}{16\,m_*^{4}\,D_A}\qquad\text{for every } C<m_* . \] Consequently the conjecture is equivalent to the statement that \[ E(C)<\frac{1}{16\,(C+1)^{4}\,D_A}\qquad\text{for every } C\ge 2^{71}. \]
results.label: rrt:thm:tail

results.name: A polynomial tail bounds the least counterexample
results.status_text: conditional on Lau's theorem (Theorem 13.1, from an unrefereed preprint), that for every t prime to 3 the integers whose orbit reaches t have lower natural density at least t^(-4)/D_A, which the book does not prove
results.conditions: Lau's theorem (Theorem 13.1, from an unrefereed preprint), that for every t prime to 3 the integers whose orbit reaches t have lower natural density at least t^(-4)/D_A, which the book does not prove.
results.summary: Granting Lau's theorem, a bound K C^(-4-epsilon) on the tail of the orbit minimum bounds any least counterexample explicitly, so the conjecture reduces to a finite computation.
results.statement: Assume Lau's theorem and suppose $E(C)\le K\,C^{-4-\varepsilon}$ for all $C\ge C_1$, with $K,\varepsilon>0$. Then any least counterexample satisfies \[ m_*\le\max\bigl\{C_1+1,\ 1+(17\,K\,D_A)^{1/\varepsilon}\bigr\}, \] so the conjecture reduces to a finite computation.
results.label: rrt:cor:poly

results.name: Cramer regime for the logarithmic multiplier of coprime Conway maps
results.summary: For a coprime Conway map with unequal multipliers and n uniform modulo d^k, the upper tail of the logarithmic multiplier has the Gaussian asymptotic with the Mills ratio factor for deviations x_k tending to infinity with x_k=o(k^(1/6)).
results.statement: Let $T$ be a coprime Conway map whose multipliers are not all equal, with drift $\mu$ and variance $\sigma^2$ of $\log(m_i/d)$ under the uniform law, and let $n$ be uniform on a complete residue system modulo $d^k$. If $x_k\to\infty$ with $x_k=o(k^{1/6})$, then \[ \mathbb{P}\bigl(\log M_k\ge k\mu+x_k\,\sigma\sqrt{k}\,\bigr)=\bigl(1+o(1)\bigr)\,\frac{e^{-x_k^2/2}}{x_k\sqrt{2\pi}} . \]
results.label: rrt:prop:cramer

results.name: Feynman and Kac recursion for the Fourier coefficients of the Syracuse variable
results.summary: The Fourier coefficient u_n(B) of the Syracuse variable at the frequency 2^B satisfies an explicit recursion from level n-1 to level n, which with a truncated window of exponents computes the table to level n in O(n^2) operations.
results.statement: $u_0\equiv1$ and, for $n\ge1$ and every integer $B$, \[ u_n(B)=\sum_{a\ge1}2^{-a}\exp\bigl(2\pi i\,2^{B-a}/3^n\bigr)\,u_{n-1}(B-a). \]
results.label: rrt:prop:fk

results.name: The Syracuse offset is Phi of the reversed word
results.summary: The offset of a word equals 3^(n-1) Phi of the reversed word over 2^(A_n), an integer over a power of two, so the Fourier phase at a power of two frequency is an ordinary real phase.
results.statement: Let $w=(a_1,\dots,a_n)$ have partial sums $A_j$ and let $\tilde w=(a_n,\dots,a_1)$. Then \[ \mathrm{off}(w)=\sum_{j=1}^n3^{j-1}2^{-A_j}=\frac{3^{n-1}\,\Phi(\tilde w)}{2^{A_n}}, \] and $3^{n-1}\Phi(\tilde w)$ is an integer. Consequently, for every word with $A_n\le k$, \[ \exp\bigl(2\pi i\,2^k\,\mathrm{off}(w)/3^n\bigr)=\exp\bigl(2\pi i\,2^{\,k-A_n}\,\Phi(\tilde w)/3\bigr), \] where the right side is an ordinary real phase.
results.label: rrt:prop:phi

results.name: Problem R1: Is there an undecidable problem inside the coprime class?
results.summary: Decide whether the coprime class of Conway maps, which preserves Haar measure, contains an undecidable problem, equivalently whether measure preservation limits computational power.
results.statement: Is there an undecidable problem inside the coprime class of Definition 20.3? Equivalently, does measure preservation limit computational power, or can a coprime Conway map simulate a universal machine on a set of measure zero?
results.label: rrt:op:undecidable

results.name: Problem R2: Almost bounded values for coprime maps
results.summary: Extend density one descent to almost bounded values in logarithmic density for every coprime Conway map with negative drift, following Tao.
results.statement: Extend Theorem 20.6 from descent below $n$ to descent to almost bounded values, in logarithmic density, for every coprime Conway map with $\mu<0$, following Tao (Tao 2022). The analogue of the Syracuse random variable lives modulo powers of the $m_i$.
results.label: rrt:prob:r2

results.name: Problem R3: The martingale family
results.summary: Decide whether the martingale family of coprime maps, whose idealized orbit is a martingale with Pareto index one, shares the backward tree structure and positive density results of the Collatz map.
results.statement: For the martingale family $\sum_i m_i=d^2$ the idealized orbit is a martingale and excursions have Pareto index one. Does this family share finer features of the Collatz map, for instance the structure of the backward tree and the positive density results of Chapter 13?
results.label: rrt:prob:r3

results.name: Problem R4: Divergence of the alternation
results.summary: Prove the analogue of Tao's theorem for the alternation of the Collatz map with a modulus three map, namely almost unbounded values in logarithmic density, and the order of the density of captured integers.
results.statement: Theorem 20.11(d) is the easy direction for the alternation $C=B_m\circ T$. Prove the analogue of Tao's theorem: for $m=19$, say, almost every positive integer, in logarithmic density, has an orbit under $C$ that attains almost unbounded values. Is the density of captured integers below $N$ of order $N^{-\theta^*_C}$?
results.label: rrt:prob:r4

results.name: Problem R5: Resonant pairs
results.summary: Classify resonant pairs of coprime Conway maps and find the invariant measure and drift of their alternation, expected to be self similar in general.
results.statement: Classify resonant pairs. For coprime Conway maps with moduli $d_A,d_B$ and a resonant multiplier, find the invariant measure on $\mathbb{Z}_{d_A}\times\mathbb{Z}_{d_B}$ of the alternation and its drift. In Theorem 20.11 that measure is Haar; in general it should be a self similar measure of the kind that appears in Tao's work.
results.label: rrt:prob:r5

results.name: Problem R6: The entropy budget
results.summary: Show with an explicit rate that the type of the first kappa log_2 N parity digits of a uniform integer up to N obeys the fair coin large deviation bound for kappa above 1, up to the full budget 4.82.
results.statement: Close the entropy budget. Let $n$ be uniform on $\{1,\dots,N\}$ and fix $\kappa>1$. Show, with an explicit rate, that the type of the first $\kappa\log_2 N$ parity digits of $n$ obeys the same large deviation bound as for fair coin flips. For $\kappa\le 1$ this is Theorem 20.4. Any $\kappa>1$ is a pseudorandomness statement beyond the seed, and the full budget is $\kappa=4.82$.
results.label: rrt:prob:r6

results.name: Problem R7: The amusical permutation
results.summary: Decide whether the orbit of 8 under Conway's amusical permutation is infinite.
results.statement: Decide whether the orbit of $8$ under Conway's amusical permutation is infinite. The map is not in the coprime class, and its parity chain, unlike that of Theorem 20.9, has not been shown to lock.
results.label: rrt:prob:r7

results.name: Problem R8: Convergence of the depth cocycle
results.summary: Prove that r^(-1) log Z_r(lambda) converges along the rungs and that the limit is differentiable in lambda.
results.statement: Prove that $r^{-1}\log Z_r(\lambda)$ converges along the rungs for every $\lambda\ge0$, and that the limit $P(\lambda)$ is differentiable. The cocycle is piecewise constant in the phase with two breakpoints, and its matrices map the positive cone strictly inside itself after boundedly many steps, so uniform convergence over the phase is plausible.
results.label: rrt:prob:r8

results.name: Problem R9: The rate near one
results.summary: Find the behaviour of the rate rho(c) as c tends to 1, conjectured of order (1-c) log(1/(1-c)).
results.statement: Find the behaviour of $\rho(c)$ as $c\to1$. A word with $\Phi\ge c\,B_r$ can leave the Christoffel word on a fraction of indices of order $1-c$, which suggests $\rho(c)$ of order $(1-c)\log\frac{1}{1-c}$.
results.label: rrt:prob:r9

results.name: Problem R10: M3 restated
results.summary: Find an inequality for integer cycles that beats the bound B_r/(3(2^delta minus 1)), which a rational cycle attains, and so must use the denominator 2^s minus 3^r.
results.statement: Restate M3 with Theorem 20.12: the target is an inequality for integer cycles that beats $M\le B_r/(3(2^{\delta}-1))$, a bound that a rational cycle attains exactly. Any such inequality must fail for the Christoffel cycle itself, so it must use the denominator $2^s-3^r$.
results.label: rrt:prob:r10

results.name: Problem R11: B2 restated
results.summary: Prove that the largest Fourier coefficient of the Syracuse variable at frequencies prime to 3 is 3^(-(eta+o(1))n) with eta=0.05004.
results.statement: Prove that $\max_{3\nmid\xi}|\widehat\pi_n(\xi)|=3^{-(\eta+o(1))n}$ with $\eta=0.05004$. The lower bound should follow from the words of Table 20.6, by Proposition 20.28 and the finitely many low levels at which they leave the real range. For the upper bound, show that the maximum over all frequencies prime to $3$ is attained at a power of two below $3^n$ for every $n$, as it is for $n\le18$.
results.label: rrt:prob:r11

results.name: Problem R12: Beyond the uniform bound
results.summary: Find the tail rate obtained by Tao's method when resonant frequencies are treated separately and the rest are bounded by their root mean square size.
results.statement: Find the tail rate that the method of Tao gives when the resonant frequencies $2^k$ with $3^n/2^{c}<2^k<3^n$ are treated separately and the remaining frequencies are bounded by their root mean square size, of order $\sqrt n\,3^{-n/2}$.
results.label: rrt:prob:r12

results.name: Problem R13: An effective basin bound
results.summary: Prove a lower bound c rho(t)/t for the density of the integers reaching t, which would give the tail criterion exponent 1 with no tower.
results.statement: Prove a lower bound for the density of the integers reaching $t$ of the form $c\,\rho(t)\,t^{-1}$, with $\rho$ the density of the Syracuse offsets at $t$ and $c$ of ordinary size. With such a bound the criterion of Theorem 20.20 has exponent $1$ and no tower.
results.label: rrt:prob:r13

results.name: Problem R14: The laboratory
results.summary: For the 3x+d maps at the rungs, measure the law of basin sizes and test whether the basin of a cycle is proportional to the sum over its elements of the off cycle share of the offset density.
results.statement: For the $3x+d$ maps with $d=2^s-3^r$ at the rungs, measure the law of basin sizes over cycles and test whether the basin of a cycle is proportional to the sum over its elements of the off cycle share of the offset density. This is a statement that can be checked exactly, and it is the $3x+d$ shadow of the effective basin bound.
results.label: rrt:prob:r14

results.name: Trajectory mixing of Syracuse residues modulo powers of 3
results.summary: Asks for a proof that, from a random starting value, the residues modulo a power of 3 along a Syracuse orbit are distributed as in the random model of the book, whose Markov chain mixes exactly; numerically, modulo 243, they approach the model law at the rate of independent sampling.
results.statement: Let $S$ be the Syracuse map on the odd positive integers, $S(y)=(3y+1)/2^{v_2(3y+1)}$, where $v_2(m)$ is the exponent of the largest power of $2$ dividing $m$, and for an odd $x_0$ let $y_j=S^{(j)}(x_0)$. Fix $a\ge1$, let $U_a$ be the residues modulo $3^a$ prime to $3$, and let $\pi_a$ be the stationary law of the Markov chain on $U_a$ that moves from $r$ to $(3r+1)2^{-K}\bmod3^a$, with $K$ an independent Geometric$(\tfrac12)$ variable, $\mathbb{P}(K=k)=2^{-k}$ for $k\ge1$. Fix a constant $C>1/|\log(3/4)|\approx3.48$ and let $x_0$ be drawn uniformly from the odd integers up to $X$. Problem: show that the empirical distribution of $y_j\bmod3^a$ over the strides before the orbit reaches $1$, stopped after $\lfloor C\log X\rfloor$ strides if the orbit has not reached $1$ by then, converges in probability to $\pi_a$ as $X\to\infty$.
results.label: prob:ch11:o2

results.name: Failure fraction of Lyapunov potentials of growing depth for the Syracuse map
results.summary: Asks how small the fraction of odd integers at which a Lyapunov potential fails can be made when the potential may read further ahead along the orbit, and whether it can be driven to zero; the answer is a question about the random model of the book, not about the arithmetic of the map.
results.statement: Let $S$ be the Syracuse map on the odd positive integers, $S(x)=(3x+1)/2^{v_2(3x+1)}$, where $v_2(m)$ is the exponent of the largest power of $2$ dividing $m$. A potential is a function $V(x)=\log x+\varphi(x)$ on the odd positive integers, and it fails at $x$ if $V(S(x))\ge V(x)$. Group the strides of an orbit into blocks, each a maximal run of strides $y\mapsto S(y)$ with $v_2(3y+1)=1$ followed by one stride with $v_2(3y+1)\ge2$; the block that starts at $x$ has $v_2(x+1)$ strides, its run length. No potential whose correction $\varphi$ depends on boundedly many binary digits of $x$ decreases at every stride, and the run length potentials $\log x+c\,v_2(x+1)$ fail at a fraction at least $0.143$ of the odd integers. Problem: for $h\ge1$, determine the infimum, over the potentials of depth $h$, whose correction reads the run lengths of the first $h$ blocks of the orbit of $x$, of the density of the odd integers at which the potential fails; decide whether it tends to $0$ as $h\to\infty$, and if so, how fast.
results.label: prob:ch11:o3p

results.name: Boundedness of the variance deficit and the third cumulant of total stopping times
results.summary: Asks for a proof that the shortfall of the variance of total stopping times against the random model, which an exact census finds to be an additive and apparently bounded term concentrated in the final descent of the orbit, stays bounded as the starting values grow, and for an explanation of their skewness, which is smaller than the model predicts.
results.statement: Let $T$ be the accelerated Collatz map, $T(n)=n/2$ for even $n$ and $T(n)=(3n+1)/2$ for odd $n$, and for $n\ge2$ whose orbit reaches $1$ let $\sigma_\infty(n)$ be the number of steps of $T$ from $n$ to $1$. For $k\ge1$ and $n$ in the dyadic block $[2^k,2^{k+1})$, let $a_{\mathrm t}(n)$ be the number of odd values among $T^{(k)}(n),\ldots,T^{(\sigma_\infty(n)-1)}(n)$ and $Z_{\mathrm t}(n)=\tfrac12\log3\,\bigl(2a_{\mathrm t}(n)-(\sigma_\infty(n)-k)\bigr)$, the centred parity sum over the steps after the first $k$. Put $\sigma^2=\tfrac14(\log3)^2$ and, with $n$ uniform on the block, define the additive variance deficit $D_{\mathrm v}(k)=\sigma^2\,\mathbb{E}(\sigma_\infty-k)-\operatorname{Var}Z_{\mathrm t}$. Problem: prove that $D_{\mathrm v}(k)$ is bounded in $k$, either assuming that every orbit reaches $1$, or unconditionally for the integers of each block whose orbits reach $1$ within a fixed multiple of $k$ steps; and explain the third cumulant: the skewness of $\sigma_\infty$ on the block is $0.67$ at $k=29$, against $0.96$ for the inverse Gaussian first passage law of the model.
results.label: prob:ch11:o4

results.name: Arithmetic sharpening of the window bound on the least element of a Collatz cycle
results.origin_text: First stated in Polson and Sokolov (2026), Five Bayesian problems raised by AlphaProof Nexus, manuscript.
results.summary: Asks for an improvement, drawn from the arithmetic of the parity vector, of the bound on the least element of a hypothetical Collatz cycle; a strong enough improvement would reduce the cycle half of the conjecture to a finite computation.
results.statement: Let $T$ be the accelerated Collatz map, $T(n)=n/2$ for even $n$ and $T(n)=(3n+1)/2$ for odd $n$. For a cycle of $T$ on the positive integers with $m$ odd steps, $k$ steps in all and least element $x_{\min}$, put $\Lambda=k\log2-m\log3>0$. Every nontrivial cycle satisfies $x_{\min}<m/(3\Lambda)$ (the window lemma of the book). Problem: find a function $f$, derived from the arithmetic of the parity vector of the cycle rather than from the size of its elements, such that every nontrivial cycle satisfies $x_{\min}<m/(3\Lambda f(m))$. A function with $f(m)\ge\frac m3(1+\eta)$ for a fixed $\eta>0$ and all large $m$ would confine the least element of every nontrivial cycle with many odd steps below a constant, about $1/(2\eta)$ for small $\eta$, and so reduce the cycle half of the Collatz conjecture to a finite verification.
results.label: prob:ch11:c1

results.name: Verification ranges that exclude the later rungs under Hercher's sharper accounting
results.summary: Asks for the computation that would extend Hercher's computer assisted exclusion of Collatz cycles of a given length to the next lengths in line, the rungs of the one sided continued fraction ladder of log2 3.
results.statement: Let $\theta=\log_23$ and, for an integer $r\ge1$, $\delta(r)=\lceil r\theta\rceil-r\theta$; the rungs of the one sided ladder of $\theta$ are the $r$ with $\delta(r)<\delta(r')$ for every $1\le r'<r$, the best one sided approximations of $\theta$ from above. Let $T$ be the accelerated Collatz map, $T(n)=n/2$ for even $n$ and $T(n)=(3n+1)/2$ for odd $n$, and call $X$ a verification range if every positive integer below $X$ reaches $1$ under $T$. Hercher (2023, Theorem 27) shows that if $X$ is a verification range, a nontrivial cycle of $T$ with $r$ odd elements and $s$ elements in all satisfies $0<s/r-\theta<1/(4X\log2)$, so that the least cycle length it does not exclude is a rung, and his computer assisted Corollary 29 shows that the verification range $3\cdot2^{69}$ already excludes cycles whose length is the rung $72\,057\,431\,991$. Problem: extend that computation to the later rungs: for each rung from $137\,528\,045\,312$ on, find the least verification range at which Hercher's accounting excludes it.
results.label: prob:ch11:c3

results.name: Bounded form of Tao's theorem: orbit minimum at most 2^71 on a set of logarithmic density one
results.summary: Asks for a proof that the least value on the orbit of n is at most 2 to the power 71 for all n in a set of logarithmic density one, a bounded form of Tao's theorem that, given the positive density theorems of Mazur and Lau, would imply the Collatz conjecture, and which the conjecture implies.
results.statement: Let $T_0$ be the Collatz map on the positive integers, $T_0(n)=n/2$ for even $n$ and $T_0(n)=3n+1$ for odd $n$, and let $\mathrm{Col}_{\min}(n)=\min_{k\ge0}T_0^{(k)}(n)$ be the least value on the orbit of $n$. A set $A$ of positive integers has logarithmic density one if $(\log x)^{-1}\sum_{n\le x,\,n\in A}1/n\to1$ as $x\to\infty$. Tao proved that for every function $f$ with $f(n)\to\infty$ one has $\mathrm{Col}_{\min}(n)<f(n)$ for all $n$ in a set of logarithmic density one, and every positive integer up to $2^{71}$ is known to reach $1$ (verification of Bařina). Problem: show that $\mathrm{Col}_{\min}(n)\le2^{71}$ for all $n$ in a set of logarithmic density one. By the verification up to $2^{71}$, if the positive density theorems of Mazur and Lau are right, this implies the Collatz conjecture, and the conjecture implies it.
results.label: prob:ch11:b1

results.name: True decay rate of the Fourier coefficients of the Syracuse random variable modulo powers of 3
results.summary: Asks how fast the largest Fourier coefficient of the Syracuse random variable modulo 3 to the power d, over frequencies prime to 3, tends to zero, choosing between decay like exp of minus c times the square of log d, like exp of minus c times d to a power gamma below 1, and eventually geometric decay.
results.statement: Let $a_1,a_2,\ldots$ be independent random variables with $\mathbb{P}(a_i=k)=2^{-k}$ for $k\ge1$, and let $\pi_d$ be the law on $\mathbb{Z}/3^d\mathbb{Z}$ of $\sum_{i=1}^{d}3^{i-1}2^{-(a_1+\cdots+a_i)}$, with $2$ inverted modulo $3^d$ (the law of Tao's Syracuse random variable modulo $3^d$). Its Fourier coefficient at the frequency $\xi$ is $\widehat\pi_d(\xi)=\sum_{y\bmod3^d}\pi_d(y)e^{-2\pi i\xi y/3^d}$. Tao proved that $\max_{3\nmid\xi}|\widehat\pi_d(\xi)|$ eventually decays faster than any power of $d$, and the exact computation of the book shows that through $d=18$ it stays between $3.6\,d^{-2}$ and $3.9\,d^{-2}$ from $d=7$ on and sits at $\xi=\pm2^k$ with $d\le k\le1.28\,d$. Problem: determine how fast $\max_{3\nmid\xi}|\widehat\pi_d(\xi)|$ tends to zero as $d\to\infty$. Is it $\exp(-c(\log d)^2)$, $\exp(-cd^{\gamma})$ for some $\gamma<1$, or eventually geometric?
results.label: prob:ch11:b2

results.name: Sharpness of Shaik's threshold 3/log(4/3) for total stopping times
results.summary: Asks for a proof that, for every constant c below 3 over log(4/3), the integers n whose total stopping time is at most c log n have natural density zero, so that the threshold of Shaik for positive density is sharp.
results.statement: Let $T_0$ be the Collatz map on the positive integers, $T_0(n)=n/2$ for even $n$ and $T_0(n)=3n+1$ for odd $n$, and let $\sigma_0(n)$ be the total stopping time of $n$, the least $k\ge0$ with $T_0^{(k)}(n)=1$ (infinite if there is none). Shaik's preprint (2026) obtains positive lower density for convergence within $c\log x$ steps of $T_0$, for the integers below $x$, for every $c>3/\log(4/3)\approx10.428$. Problem: show that for every $c<3/\log(4/3)$ the set of $n$ with $\sigma_0(n)\le c\log n$ has natural density zero, so that Shaik's threshold is sharp. A renewal calculation in the book predicts that below the threshold the share of $n$ meeting the bound tends to zero.
results.label: prob:ch11:b3

results.name: Exact worst case function gap rate of Switching MM for small condition numbers
results.summary: The worst case rate of Switching MM is known exactly for the distance to the minimizer, and for the function gap on ill conditioned problems; the problem asks for the exact function gap rate, and the function that attains it, on well conditioned problems, where numerical performance estimation shows that the known bound is not tight.
results.statement: Let $f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ be $\mu$ strongly convex and $L$ smooth, with $\kappa=L/\mu$, let $0\le\beta<1$, and let $G=\nabla f$. Switching MM with deterministic parity injection and step $\alpha$, started at $x_{-1}=x_0$, takes the gradient step $x_{t+1}=x_t-\alpha G(x_t)$ at even $t$ and, at odd $t$, $y_t=x_t+\beta(x_t-x_{t-1})$ and $x_{t+1}=y_t-\alpha G(y_t)$, here with $\alpha=1/L$. Its even iterates contract the distance to the minimizer by $q=(1-1/\kappa)\max\bigl(1-(1+\beta)/\kappa,\beta\bigr)$ per period of two steps, which is the exact worst case over the class, and the function gap contracts by $q^2$ per period, which is exact for $\kappa\ge(1+\beta)/(1-\beta)$. Problem: for $\kappa<(1+\beta)/(1-\beta)$, where performance estimation gives a smaller worst case (for example $0.049$ against $q^2=0.086$ at $\beta=\log_23-1$ and $\kappa=2$), find the exact worst case contraction of the function gap per period in closed form and describe the function that attains it.
results.label: prob:ch11:s1

results.name: Five thirds noise bound of Switching MM beyond quadratics
results.summary: Asks to extend the proven robustness of Switching MM to gradient noise, a stationary error at most five thirds of that of gradient descent for every momentum coefficient below one, from quadratic objectives to all smooth strongly convex objectives.
results.statement: Let $f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ be $\mu$ strongly convex and $L$ smooth, accessed through a stochastic gradient oracle $G(x)=\nabla f(x)+\xi$ whose noise $\xi$ is fresh at every call, has mean zero and bounded variance, and let $0\le\beta<1$. Switching MM with deterministic parity injection and step $\alpha$, started at $x_{-1}=x_0$, takes the gradient step $x_{t+1}=x_t-\alpha G(x_t)$ at even $t$ and, at odd $t$, $y_t=x_t+\beta(x_t-x_{t-1})$ and $x_{t+1}=y_t-\alpha G(y_t)$. For quadratic objectives with additive noise of covariance $\sigma^2I$, the book proves that on every eigendirection with normalized step at most $1$ the stationary variance of this method is at most $\beta+2/(2+\beta)<\tfrac53$ times that of gradient descent with the same step. Problem: show that for every such $f$ and every $\beta<1$, the stationary mean square error of this method is at most $\tfrac53$ times that of gradient descent with the same step, up to terms that vanish with the step size.
results.label: prob:ch11:s2

results.name: A principled adaptive switching rule for Switching MM
results.summary: Asks for a rule, using only the smoothness constant and observed function values, that decides when Switching MM injects momentum, keeping its proven robustness to gradient noise while matching the speed of momentum applied at every step on noiseless problems.
results.statement: Let $f$ be an $L$ smooth objective. Switching MM alternates plain gradient steps $x_{t+1}=x_t-\alpha\nabla f(x_t)$ with momentum injection steps $y_t=x_t+\beta(x_t-x_{t-1})$, $x_{t+1}=y_t-\alpha\nabla f(y_t)$; with deterministic parity injection (an injection at every odd $t$) its stationary variance under additive gradient noise is, on quadratics and at steps up to $1/L$, at most $\tfrac53$ times that of gradient descent with the same step, uniformly in $0\le\beta<1$, but in the absence of noise it converges more slowly than momentum applied at every step, and its adaptive variant injects only when the most recent reduction of a merit gap was inadequate. Problem: find a principled switching rule, using only $L$ and observed function values, that retains that uniform noise bound while closing the noiseless gap to momentum applied at every step.
results.label: prob:ch11:s4
